payload.detail: thm:sharp-effect-frontier carries a disposition outside its exact dependency rewire

proofs.proof_tex:
The anchor assumptions make \((n,C,\varepsilon)\) an irreducible ICA representation of \(P_X\). We first prove that \(J_x(C)\) is nonempty, which also supplies at least one completion through the witness lemma. Extend the full-row-rank matrix \(C\) to \(T_0\in\operatorname{GL}_n(\mathbb R)\), with \((T_0)_{\mathsf O,:}=C\), and write \(W_0=T_0^{-1}\). The \((x,x)\) entry of \(T_0W_0=I_n\) is
\[
 1=\sum_{j=1}^n C_{xj}(W_0)_{jx}. \tag{32}
\]
Thus some \(j\) satisfies \(C_{xj}(W_0)_{jx}\ne0\). The inverse-cofactor identity gives
\[
 (W_0)_{jx}=\frac{(-1)^{x+j}\det((T_0)_{-x,-j})}{\det(T_0)}, \tag{33}
\]
so \((T_0)_{-x,-j}\) is nonsingular. Its \(p-1\) observed rows are \(C_{-x,-j}\); they are linearly independent, whence \(\operatorname{rank}(C_{-x,-j})=p-1\). Together with \(C_{xj}\ne0\), this proves \(j\in J_x(C)\).

Take an arbitrary \(\mathcal M\in\mathfrak F_x(P_X)\). The law-fiber response-and-rank lemma supplies a matched anchor source \(j\in J_x(C)\) and proves
\[
 \boldsymbol\theta_{-x\leftarrow x}(\mathcal M)
 =\frac{C_{-x,j}}{C_{xj}}
 \in\mathcal R_x^{\mathrm{vec}}(C). \tag{34}
\]
It also proves, by the cited irreducible-ICA theorem, that the completion source count is \(n\) and its observed mixing is \(C\Pi D\). This proves the first inclusion and the claimed invariance across the entire observational-law fiber, not merely across a fixed source representation.

Conversely, let \(r=C_{-x,j}/C_{xj}\in\mathcal R_x^{\mathrm{vec}}(C)\). The canonical witness lemma returns \(\mathcal M_j\in\mathfrak F_x(P_X)\) and gives \(\boldsymbol\theta_{-x\leftarrow x}(\mathcal M_j)=r\). Hence every frontier point is attained by a full same-law structural completion. The two inclusions prove the vector equality. Taking coordinate \(y\) in (34) and in every witness proves the scalar equality; it is a projection of the same completion-wise vector set, not a Cartesian recombination across outcomes.

For complexity, Gaussian elimination extends the rows of \(C\) and inverts \(T_0\) in \(O(n^3)\) arithmetic operations. Equivalence (16) scans the rows of \(W_0\) and classifies all admissible columns in \(O(n^2)\) additional operations. For each of at most \(n\) admissible sources, the shear is \(O(n^2)\), an augmenting-path algorithm finds the complementary perfect matching in \(O(n^3)\), and row normalization is \(O(n^2)\). Thus all full witnesses cost \(O(n^4)\). Exact zero tests are part of the real-arithmetic model; no floating-point or bit-complexity claim is made. Each vector point has its indexed witness, and selecting one index for every distinct scalar projection yields one exact witness per scalar value.

By the sharp-frontier theorem, the image of the full response-vector target over \(\mathfrak F_x(P_X)\) is the nonempty set \(\mathcal R_x^{\mathrm{vec}}(C)\). Identification therefore means exactly that this set is a singleton. If two indices \(j,k\in J_x(C)\) produced the same vector, then their nonzero treatment entries would give
\[
 \frac{C_{-x,j}}{C_{xj}}=\frac{C_{-x,k}}{C_{xk}}. \tag{35}
\]
Adjoining the common \(x\)-coordinate \(1\) to both sides of (35) yields \(c_j/C_{xj}=c_k/C_{xk}\), so \(c_j\) and \(c_k\) are proportional. Pairwise nonproportionality forces \(j=k\). Hence the map \(j\mapsto C_{-x,j}/C_{xj}\) is injective on \(J_x(C)\), and
\[
 |\mathcal R_x^{\mathrm{vec}}(C)|=|J_x(C)|. \tag{36}
\]
This proves the vector criterion.

For the scalar criterion, every \(j\in J_x(C)\) has \(C_{xj}\ne0\), so the \(x\)-row of \(C_{\{x,y\},J_x(C)}\) is nonzero. This two-row matrix has rank one exactly when all its two-column determinants vanish:
\[
 C_{xj}C_{yk}-C_{xk}C_{yj}=0
 \quad\text{for all }j,k\in J_x(C). \tag{37}
\]
Division by the nonzero product \(C_{xj}C_{xk}\) makes (37) equivalent to
\[
 \frac{C_{yj}}{C_{xj}}=\frac{C_{yk}}{C_{xk}}
 \quad\text{for all }j,k\in J_x(C), \tag{38}
\]
which is precisely \(|\mathcal R_{xy}(C)|=1\). The scalar part of the sharp theorem identifies this with scalar causal identification.

If \(|J_x(C)|>1\), choose distinct \(j,k\in J_x(C)\). Equation (36) says their response vectors differ. The canonical witness lemma returns \(\mathcal M_j,\mathcal M_k\in\mathfrak F_x(P_X)\) realizing those two vectors. If instead the scalar rank condition fails, (37) supplies a pair whose scalar ratios differ, and the same two witnesses realize the distinct scalar responses. After the shared \(O(n^3)\) basis extension and inverse, each of two shears, complementary matchings, and row normalizations costs \(O(n^3)\), proving the additional-operation claim.

Fix \(\zeta=(P_X,C,\varepsilon,\lambda)\in\mathfrak P_{p,n,r}(a,\delta,\sigma,\kappa,\Lambda,M)\). Unit normalization gives
\[
 \lVert X\rVert_2\le\sum_{j=1}^n|\varepsilon_j|.
\]
For nonnegative \(t_j\), convexity gives \((\sum_jt_j)^{2r}\le n^{2r-1}\sum_jt_j^{2r}\). The source-moment envelope therefore implies
\[
 \mathbb E\lVert X\rVert_2^{2r}
 \le n^{2r-1}\sum_{j=1}^n\mathbb E|\varepsilon_j|^{2r}
 \le n^{2r}M=H. \tag{39}
\]
Let \(\mu\in\mathbb R^m\) collect all nonconstant raw moments through degree \(r\), and let \(\widetilde\mu\) collect their untrimmed empirical averages. If a coordinate has degree at most \(r\), its squared monomial is at most \(1+\lVert X\rVert_2^{2r}\). Independence of the \(N\) observations and (39) give
\[
 \mathbb E\lVert\widetilde\mu-\mu\rVert_2^2
 \le\frac{m(1+H)}{N}. \tag{40}
\]
Every true moment coordinate has absolute value at most \((1+H)^{1/2}\le1+H=B_m\). Coordinatewise clipping to \([-B_m,B_m]\) is projection onto an interval containing that true coordinate and cannot increase Euclidean error. Hence, by \(P(Z>t)\le\mathbb E Z/t\) for the nonnegative variable \(Z=\lVert\widehat\mu-\mu\rVert_2^2\),
\[
 E_N=\{\lVert\widehat\mu-\mu\rVert_2\le e_N\},
 \qquad
 \inf_{\zeta\in\mathfrak P_{p,n,r}}P_X^{\otimes N}(E_N)\ge1-\alpha. \tag{41}
\]

For an ordered tensor coordinate, the moment--cumulant identity is
\[
 \operatorname{cum}(X_{i_1},\ldots,X_{i_r})
 =\sum_{\pi\in\mathfrak P_r}(-1)^{|\pi|-1}(|\pi|-1)!
 \prod_{A\in\pi}\mathbb E\!\left[\prod_{k\in A}X_{i_k}\right]. \tag{42}
\]
On \([-B_m,B_m]^m\), telescoping a product of \(|\pi|\) factors bounds its change by \(|\pi|B_m^{|\pi|-1}\lVert\widehat\mu-\mu\rVert_2\). Summing (42) and then the squares of its \(p^r\) ordered coordinates gives, on \(E_N\),
\[
 \lVert\widehat{\mathcal T}_r-\mathcal T_r\rVert_F
 \le p^{r/2}\sum_{\pi\in\mathfrak P_r}(|\pi|-1)!|\pi|B_m^{|\pi|-1}e_N
 =\tau_N. \tag{43}
\]

The true factor pair is feasible for the minimum-distance problem. The numerical feasible set is compact: normalized columns range over a product of unit spheres, cumulants range over the compact set \(\{t:\kappa\le|t|\le\Lambda\}\), and the loading, singular-value, and pencil-gap alternatives are closed. Its nonemptiness is assumed. A continuous objective therefore has a minimizer; successive minimization of its finitely many coordinates over the compact argmin set defines the stated lexicographic selection. Optimality and (43) imply
\[
 \left\lVert\sum_{j=1}^n\widehat\lambda_j\widehat c_j^{\otimes r}-\mathcal T_r\right\rVert_F
 \le2\tau_N. \tag{44}
\]
The numerical pencil-inverse lemma applies directly to the fitted and true factor pairs. If \(2\tau_N<\epsilon_0\), it supplies one common permutation for which
\[
 \lVert\widehat C-C\rVert_F\le2L_C\tau_N=b_N. \tag{45}
\]

Assume also \(b_N<\min\{a,\delta\}/2\). Both feasible matrices obey the alternative that each loading is either zero or has magnitude at least \(a\). A zero entry in one matrix paired with a nonzero entry in the other would make the Frobenius distance at least \(a\), contradicting (45); hence their zero patterns agree. For a deletion matrix \(G\) with \(p-1\) rows, its least singular value satisfies
\[
 s_{\min}(G)=\inf_{\lVert z\rVert_2=1}\lVert G^\top z\rVert_2.
\]
The triangle inequality therefore gives \(|s_{\min}(G')-s_{\min}(G)|\le\lVert G'-G\rVert_{\mathrm{op}}\). Applied to every deletion pair and then bounded by (45), this difference is less than \(\delta/2\). Since each feasible deletion singular value is either zero or at least \(\delta\), their zero statuses agree. Consequently
\[
 \widehat J_x=J_x(C) \tag{46}
\]
simultaneously for every observed \(x\), after the same common source permutation.

For \(j\in J_x(C)=\widehat J_x\), both denominators have magnitude at least \(a\), unit normalization gives \(|C_{ij}|\le1\), and (45) bounds every coordinate error by \(b_N\). Thus, for every \(i\ne x\),
\[
 \left|\frac{\widehat C_{ij}}{\widehat C_{xj}}-
 \frac{C_{ij}}{C_{xj}}\right|
 \le\frac{|\widehat C_{ij}-C_{ij}|}{|\widehat C_{xj}|}
 +\frac{|C_{ij}|\,|\widehat C_{xj}-C_{xj}|}
 {|\widehat C_{xj}|\,|C_{xj}|}
 \le(a^{-1}+a^{-2})b_N=w_N. \tag{47}
\]
Taking the Euclidean norm of the \(p-1\) inequalities in (47) gives
\[
 \left\lVert\frac{\widehat C_{-x,j}}{\widehat C_{xj}}-
 \frac{C_{-x,j}}{C_{xj}}\right\rVert_2
 \le\sqrt{p-1}\,w_N=w_N^{\mathrm{vec}}. \tag{48}
\]
Therefore every true response vector lies in its corresponding confidence ball. Conversely, every point of that ball is at distance at most \(w_N^{\mathrm{vec}}\) from its estimated center and, by (48), at most another \(w_N^{\mathrm{vec}}\) from the corresponding true vector. Hence
\[
 \mathcal R_x^{\mathrm{vec}}(C)\subseteq\mathcal U_x^{\mathrm{vec}},
 \qquad
 d_H(\mathcal U_x^{\mathrm{vec}},\mathcal R_x^{\mathrm{vec}}(C))
 \le2w_N^{\mathrm{vec}}. \tag{49}
\]
The same argument in coordinate \(y\) gives the scalar inclusion and the bound \(2w_N\). Because every ball in (49) is indexed by one source and contains its entire estimated response vector, no false cross-outcome Cartesian combination is introduced.

If either informative-regime inequality fails, the fallback vector ball has radius \(\sqrt{p-1}/a\). Every admissible true vector belongs to it because all \(p-1\) numerators have magnitude at most one and the denominator has magnitude at least \(a\). The scalar fallback interval is covered by the same coordinate bound. Thus coverage holds in both regimes on the single event \(E_N\), simultaneously for all ordered queries, and (41) proves the displayed uniform probability inequality. The sharp-effect-frontier theorem equates these observable frontiers with the full observational-law-fiber causal targets. Finally, with dimensions, margins, \(M\), and \(\alpha\) fixed, \(L_m,L_C,H\) are constants, so \(\tau_N=O(N^{-1/2})\), \(2w_N=O(N^{-1/2})\), and \(2w_N^{\mathrm{vec}}=O(N^{-1/2})\).

For every order \(\nu\), write \(\lambda_{j,\nu}=\operatorname{cum}_\nu(\varepsilon_j)\). Moment determinacy presupposes finite moments of every order. Mutual independence makes mixed source cumulants vanish, while multilinearity of cumulants gives the observable tensor
\[
 \mathcal T_\nu=\operatorname{cum}_\nu(X)
 =\sum_{j=1}^n\lambda_{j,\nu}c_j^{\otimes\nu}. \tag{50}
\]
Let \(A_\nu=\{j:\lambda_{j,\nu}\ne0\}\) and \(R_\nu=|A_\nu|\). Suppose first that \(R_\nu\ge2\) and \(\nu\ge2R_\nu-1\). Put
\[
 \ell_1=\ell_2=R_\nu-1,
 \qquad
 \ell_3=\nu-2R_\nu+2\ge1. \tag{51}
\]
Reshaping (50) into these three blocks yields
\[
 \widetilde{\mathcal T}_\nu
 =\sum_{j\in A_\nu}\lambda_{j,\nu}
 \operatorname{vec}(c_j^{\otimes\ell_1})\otimes
 \operatorname{vec}(c_j^{\otimes\ell_2})\otimes
 \operatorname{vec}(c_j^{\otimes\ell_3}). \tag{52}
\]
The Veronese--Lagrange rank lemma applies to each of the first two factors because \(\ell_1=\ell_2=R_\nu-1\); their Kruskal ranks equal \(R_\nu\). Any two columns of the third factor are linearly independent: applying the same lemma to that pair uses only \(\ell_3\ge1\). Hence its Kruskal rank is at least two. Therefore
\[
 k_1+k_2+k_3\ge R_\nu+R_\nu+2=2R_\nu+2. \tag{53}
\]
The established Kruskal three-factor uniqueness lemma applied to (52) proves essential uniqueness up to a common permutation and reciprocal nonzero scalings. The tensor rank is exactly \(R_\nu\): the first factor matrix has full column rank, and the Khatri--Rao product of the second and third factors has full column rank. For the latter claim, apply a left-inverse row selecting one column of the second factor to a linear dependence among the Khatri--Rao columns; the selected nonzero third-factor column forces that coefficient to vanish, and repeat for every column. Thus the mode-one matricization has rank \(R_\nu\), furnishing the matching lower bound on tensor rank. If \(R_\nu=1\), a nonzero tensor in (50) is rank one and its common projective preimage is immediate; if \(R_\nu=0\), the tensor is zero and contributes no direction. This proves the adaptive elbow \(\nu\ge2R_\nu-1\).

For a recovery rule that knows \(n\) but not \(R_\nu\), take any \(\nu\ge2n-1\) and use the fixed degrees
\[
 (\ell_1,\ell_2,\ell_3)=(n-1,n-1,\nu-2n+2). \tag{54}
\]
For every active rank \(R_\nu\le n\), the first two degrees are at least \(R_\nu-1\), while the third is at least one. The argument (52)--(53) therefore applies unchanged. A computable exact population operation is the following constrained decomposition: minimize \(R\in\{0,\ldots,n\}\) over nonzero coefficients \(\gamma_1,\ldots,\gamma_R\), nonzero vectors \(z_1,\ldots,z_R\in\mathbb R^p\), and block factors \(b_{s\ell}\), subject to
\[
 \widetilde{\mathcal T}_\nu
 =\sum_{\ell=1}^R\gamma_\ell b_{1\ell}\otimes b_{2\ell}\otimes b_{3\ell},
 \qquad
 b_{s\ell}=\operatorname{vec}(z_\ell^{\otimes\ell_s})
 \quad(s=1,2,3). \tag{55}
\]
Equations (52)--(54), minimality, and Kruskal uniqueness prove that the solutions of (55) return exactly \(\{[c_j]:j\in A_\nu\}\). The Veronese map has no extra real projective collision: if \(z^{\otimes s}\) and \(w^{\otimes s}\) are proportional for \(s\ge1\) while \(z,w\) are not, choose a linear functional vanishing on \(w\) but not on \(z\) and contract all \(s\) modes, a contradiction.

By the established Marcinkiewicz cumulant-tail lemma, each nondegenerate non-Gaussian source with all moments has infinitely many nonzero cumulants of order at least three. Consequently, for every source \(j\), there is some \(\nu_j\ge2n-1\) with \(\lambda_{j,\nu_j}\ne0\). Since there are finitely many sources,
\[
 K_{C,\varepsilon}=\max_{1\le j\le n}\nu_j<\infty. \tag{56}
\]
Starting at \(2n-1\), solve (55) and take the set-theoretic union of its recovered projective directions. Pairwise nonproportionality prevents merging, and the rule stops when the union reaches its known cardinality \(n\), no later than (56). Labels need not be transported across orders. Ratios and deletion ranks are unchanged by nonzero column scaling and permutation, so the vector frontier and every scalar projection are then computed from the recovered projective columns. The sharp-effect-frontier theorem proves that these observable maps equal the full observational-law-fiber causal targets.

We now prove that neither the stopping order nor inference can be uniform under only the qualitative source assumptions. Fix any finite \(K\ge3\) and \(0<\gamma<\pi/4\). The established finite-moment near-Gaussian witness supplies a centered variance-one, non-Gaussian, moment-determinate law \(F\) whose first \(K\) moments equal the Gaussian moments. Give two independent sources law \(F\), and use
\[
 C_0=I_2,
 \qquad
 C_1=\begin{pmatrix}\cos\gamma&-\sin\gamma\\
 \sin\gamma&\cos\gamma\end{pmatrix}. \tag{57}
\]
The two matrices have normalized, nonzero, pairwise nonproportional columns. Independence makes every joint source moment through total degree \(K\) equal its Gaussian counterpart, and orthogonal invariance of the standard bivariate Gaussian then makes the observed moments, hence cumulants, through order \(K\) identical under \(C_0\) and \(C_1\). Their projective direction sets differ by the fixed angle \(\gamma\). Therefore no inverse with a uniformly fixed finite maximum order can recover every member of the qualitative class.

For the sampling obstruction, for each \(N\) apply the near-Gaussian witness with any order at least three and with \(d_{\mathrm{TV}}(F_N,\Phi)\le1/(4N^2)\), where \(\Phi=\mathcal N(0,1)\). Let \(P_{0,N}\) and \(P_{1,N}\) be the observed laws under (57) with independent \(F_N\) sources. Total variation contracts under a measurable map and satisfies the two-factor telescoping bound. Both orthogonal images of \(\Phi^{\otimes2}\) equal \(\mathcal N(0,I_2)\), so
\[
 d_{\mathrm{TV}}(P_{0,N},P_{1,N})
 \le4d_{\mathrm{TV}}(F_N,\Phi)\le N^{-2}. \tag{58}
\]
The analogous \(N\)-factor telescoping bound yields
\[
 d_{\mathrm{TV}}(P_{0,N}^{\otimes N},P_{1,N}^{\otimes N})
 \le N^{-1}\longrightarrow0. \tag{59}
\]
If an estimator of the direction set were uniformly consistent, assigning its output to the nearer of the two fixed projective sets in (57) would produce a test with both errors tending to zero. But for every test region \(E\), the definition of total variation gives
\[
 P_{0,N}^{\otimes N}(E^c)+P_{1,N}^{\otimes N}(E)
 \ge1-d_{\mathrm{TV}}(P_{0,N}^{\otimes N},P_{1,N}^{\otimes N})\longrightarrow1, \tag{60}
\]
a contradiction.

The causal response frontiers are separated too. For treatment \(x=1\), direct evaluation of the one-by-one deletion minors gives
\[
 \mathcal R_1^{\mathrm{vec}}(C_0)=\{0\},
 \qquad
 \mathcal R_1^{\mathrm{vec}}(C_1)=\{\tan\gamma,-\cot\gamma\}. \tag{61}
\]
Thus the same nearest-target test rules out uniform Hausdorff consistency for the frontier. More precisely, let \(\mathscr C_N\) be a random collection of compact frontier sets, let coverage mean that the true frontier belongs to \(\mathscr C_N\), and measure its uncertainty by \(\operatorname{diam}_H(\mathscr C_N)=\sup_{R,R'\in\mathscr C_N}d_H(R,R')\). If uniform coverage is \(1-\alpha\) with \(\alpha<1/2\), then under the first experiment \(\mathscr C_N\) contains the first frontier with probability at least \(1-\alpha\). By (59), it contains the second frontier under that same experiment with probability at least \(1-\alpha-o(1)\). Both events therefore occur with probability at least \(1-2\alpha-o(1)>0\). On their intersection, \(\operatorname{diam}_H(\mathscr C_N)\) is at least the fixed positive distance between the two sets in (61), contradicting uniformly vanishing Hausdorff uncertainty.

Finally, the causal map itself is discontinuous without denominator and deletion-rank margins. After nonzero column normalization, for
\[
 D_t=\begin{pmatrix}t&1\\1&1\end{pmatrix},\qquad t\to0,
\]
one has \(\mathcal R_{12}(D_t)=\{1/t,1\}\) for \(t\ne0,1\), whereas \(\mathcal R_{12}(D_0)=\{1\}\). For
\[
 E_0=\begin{pmatrix}1&1&0&1\\1&0&0&0\\0&0&1&1\end{pmatrix}
\]
and \(E_t\) obtained by replacing entry \((2,2)\) by \(t\ne0\), direct deletion-rank calculation gives \(\mathcal R_{12}(E_0)=\{0\}\) but \(\mathcal R_{12}(E_t)=\{0,t,1\}\). These matrices retain full row rank and nonzero pairwise nonproportional columns near zero. Since scalar frontiers are coordinate projections of vector frontiers, both examples also obstruct a uniform vector modulus. Quantitative lower cumulants, moments, Veronese conditioning, angular and pencil separation, deletion ranks, and denominators are therefore genuinely required for robust finite-order inference. The proved common-order theorem imposes precisely such margins and hence retains its simultaneous scalar/vector coverage and root-\(N\) Hausdorff rates.

added_lemmas.statement: Suppose that \((n,C,\varepsilon)\) is an irreducible ICA representation of \(P_X\), every coordinate of \(\varepsilon\) is non-Gaussian, and \((m_{\mathcal M},A^{\mathcal M},\xi^{\mathcal M})\in\mathfrak I(P_X)\) is any other irreducible ICA representation. Then \(m_{\mathcal M}=n\), every column of \(A^{\mathcal M}\) is proportional to exactly one column of \(C\) and conversely, and every coordinate of \(\xi^{\mathcal M}\) is non-Gaussian. Equivalently, there are an \(n\)-by-\(n\) permutation matrix \(\Pi\) and a nonsingular diagonal matrix \(D\) such that \(A^{\mathcal M}=C\Pi D\).

source.locator: Appendix B.1, Lemma 11 (Identifiability of ICA), restating Eriksson and Koivunen (2004)

attestation.note: Transcribed from Appendix B.1, Lemma 11 of the stable arXiv carrier; its three conclusions are equality of source counts, mutual proportional-column correspondence, and non-Gaussianity of the alternative sources. The matrix form with a permutation and nonsingular diagonal is the equivalent notation for that bijective correspondence.

added_lemmas.statement: Let \(A\in\mathbb R^{p\times n}\) satisfy \(A=C\Pi D\), where \(\Pi\) is a permutation matrix and \(D\) is nonsingular diagonal. If \(\pi\) is defined by \(A_{:,k}=D_{kk}C_{:,\pi(k)}\), then \(k\in J_x(A)\) if and only if \(\pi(k)\in J_x(C)\), and, whenever these conditions hold, \(A_{-x,k}/A_{xk}=C_{-x,\pi(k)}/C_{x,\pi(k)}\) and \(A_{yk}/A_{xk}=C_{y,\pi(k)}/C_{x,\pi(k)}\). Consequently \(\mathcal R_x^{\mathrm{vec}}(A)=\mathcal R_x^{\mathrm{vec}}(C)\) and \(\mathcal R_{xy}(A)=\mathcal R_{xy}(C)\).

For every \(\mathcal M\in\mathfrak F_x(P_X)\), one has \(m_{\mathcal M}=n\) and \(A^{\mathcal M}=C\Pi D\) for some permutation matrix \(\Pi\) and nonsingular diagonal matrix \(D\). If \(k=s_{\mathcal M}(x)\) and \(j=\pi(k)\) is its matched anchor source, then \(j\in J_x(C)\) and
\[
 \boldsymbol\theta_{-x\leftarrow x}(\mathcal M)
 =\frac{A^{\mathcal M}_{-x,k}}{A^{\mathcal M}_{xk}}
 =\frac{C_{-x,j}}{C_{xj}},
 \qquad
 \theta_{y\leftarrow x}(\mathcal M)=\frac{C_{yj}}{C_{xj}}.
\]
added_lemmas.proof_tex:
Fix \(\mathcal M=(m_{\mathcal M},Q,H,\xi^{\mathcal M})\in\mathfrak F_x(P_X)\), and abbreviate
\[
 T=Q^{-1}H,
 \qquad W=T^{-1}=H^{-1}Q,
 \qquad A=A^{\mathcal M}=T_{\mathsf O,:}. \tag{5}
\]
All inverses in (5) exist: \(Q\) is nonsingular by observational solvability, and a monomial matrix \(H\) is nonsingular because each of its unique row and column entries is nonzero. Let \(k=s_{\mathcal M}(x)\). By the definition of a monomial assignment there is an \(h\ne0\) such that
\[
 H_{:,k}=h e_x,
 \qquad e_k^\top H^{-1}=h^{-1}e_x^\top. \tag{6}
\]
The unit structural diagonal and (5)--(6) imply
\[
 W_{kx}=h^{-1}Q_{xx}=h^{-1}\ne0. \tag{7}
\]
The inverse-cofactor identity applied to \(W=T^{-1}\) gives
\[
 W_{kx}=\frac{(-1)^{k+x}\det(T_{-x,-k})}{\det(T)}. \tag{8}
\]
Thus \(T_{-x,-k}\) is nonsingular. Its observed rows other than \(x\) are exactly \(A_{-x,-k}\); a subset of the rows of a nonsingular matrix is linearly independent, and therefore
\[
 \operatorname{rank}(A_{-x,-k})=p-1. \tag{9}
\]

Next, (6) gives \(T_{:,k}=hQ^{-1}e_x\), hence
\[
 A_{xk}=h(Q^{-1})_{xx}. \tag{10}
\]
The principal cofactor identity is
\[
 \det(Q_{-x,-x})=\det(Q)(Q^{-1})_{xx}. \tag{11}
\]
Both determinants on the left and the first determinant on the right are nonzero by the two solvability conditions in the definition of \(\mathfrak F_x(P_X)\). Consequently \((Q^{-1})_{xx}\ne0\), and (10) gives \(A_{xk}\ne0\). Equations (9)--(10) show \(k\in J_x(A)\).

To compute the intervention response, replace the \(x\)-th structural equation by \(V_x=t\). For every row other than \(x\), differentiation of \(QV=H\xi^{\mathcal M}\) with respect to \(t\) gives
\[
 Q_{-x,-x}\frac{\partial V_{-x}}{\partial t}=-Q_{-x,x}. \tag{12}
\]
Postintervention solvability permits inversion. On the other hand, the rows other than \(x\) of \(Q(Q^{-1})_{:,x}=e_x\) give
\[
 Q_{-x,-x}(Q^{-1})_{-x,x}=-Q_{-x,x}(Q^{-1})_{xx}. \tag{13}
\]
Division by the nonzero \((Q^{-1})_{xx}\) and comparison of (12)--(13) yield
\[
 \boldsymbol\theta_{-x\leftarrow x}(\mathcal M)
 =\frac{(Q^{-1})_{\mathsf O\setminus\{x\},x}}{(Q^{-1})_{xx}}
 =\frac{A_{-x,k}}{A_{xk}}, \tag{14}
\]
where the last equality uses \(A_{:,k}=h(Q^{-1})_{\mathsf O,x}\). Coordinate \(y\) gives the scalar response.

The anchor assumptions make \((n,C,\varepsilon)\) an irreducible ICA representation of \(P_X\): its sources are mutually independent and nondegenerate, its columns are nonzero and pairwise nonproportional, and every anchor source is non-Gaussian. Membership of \(\mathcal M\) makes \((m_{\mathcal M},A,\xi^{\mathcal M})\) another irreducible representation of the same law. The cited irreducible-ICA uniqueness lemma therefore gives \(m_{\mathcal M}=n\) and \(A=C\Pi D\). Apply the monomial-invariance lemma to the admissible index \(k\). If \(j=\pi(k)\), then \(j\in J_x(C)\), and substituting (4) into (14) proves both displayed response formulas.

added_lemmas.statement:
For every \(j\in J_x(C)\), \(\operatorname{Cert}(C,x)\) returns \(\mathcal M_j\in\mathfrak F_x(P_X)\) with \(m_{\mathcal M_j}=n\), \(s_{\mathcal M_j}(x)=j\), and
\[
 \boldsymbol\theta_{-x\leftarrow x}(\mathcal M_j)=\frac{C_{-x,j}}{C_{xj}}.
\]
If \(C\) is rational, its returned matrices \(Q_j\) and \(H_j\) are rational.
added_lemmas.proof_tex:
Full row rank permits extending the \(p\) rows of \(C\) to a basis \(T_0\in\operatorname{GL}_n(\mathbb R)\); write \(W_0=T_0^{-1}\). The rows of \(C_{-x,:}\) are independent. For a fixed column \(j\), restriction of those rows to all coordinates other than \(j\) loses rank precisely when a nonzero linear combination is supported only on coordinate \(j\). Hence
\[
 \operatorname{rank}(C_{-x,-j})<p-1
 \quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad
 e_j^\top\in\operatorname{rowspan}(C_{-x,:}). \tag{15}
\]
The coefficients of \(e_j^\top\) in the row basis \(T_0\) form the row \(e_j^\top W_0\). Since the rows of \(T_0\) indexed by \(\mathsf O\) are the rows of \(C\), (15) becomes
\[
 \operatorname{rank}(C_{-x,-j})<p-1
 \quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad
 (W_0)_{jx}=0\ \text{ and }\ (W_0)_{j\ell}=0
 \text{ for every }\ell\in\mathsf L. \tag{16}
\]

Now let \(j\in J_x(C)\). If \((W_0)_{jx}\ne0\), put \(T_j=T_0\) and \(W_j=W_0\). Otherwise, (16) and the full deletion rank supply \(\ell\in\mathsf L\) with \((W_0)_{j\ell}\ne0\). Define
\[
 T_j=(I_n+e_\ell e_x^\top)T_0,
 \qquad
 W_j=W_0(I_n-e_\ell e_x^\top). \tag{17}
\]
Because \(\ell\ne x\), the two shear matrices in (17) are inverse. The shear changes only latent row \(\ell\), so \((T_j)_{\mathsf O,:}=C\), and
\[
 (W_j)_{jx}=-(W_0)_{j\ell}\ne0. \tag{18}
\]
In the square case \(n=p\), the latent set is empty and (16) shows directly that the first case must hold.

Admissibility also gives \(C_{xj}\ne0\). Since \(W_j^{-1}=T_j\), the inverse-cofactor identity now gives
\[
 (-1)^{j+x}\det((W_j)_{-j,-x})
 =\operatorname{cof}(W_j)_{jx}
 =\det(W_j)(T_j)_{xj}
 =\det(W_j)C_{xj}\ne0. \tag{19}
\]
At least one term in the determinant expansion of the complementary matrix in (19) is nonzero. Its positions form a perfect matching between all rows other than \(j\) and all columns other than \(x\). Augment this matching by assigning row \(j\) to column \(x\), and let \(\Pi_j\) permute rows according to this assignment. Every diagonal entry of \(\Pi_jW_j\) is nonzero. Therefore
\[
 D_j=\operatorname{diag}(\Pi_jW_j),
 \qquad
 Q_j=D_j^{-1}\Pi_jW_j,
 \qquad
 H_j=D_j^{-1}\Pi_j \tag{20}
\]
are well defined. The matrix \(Q_j\) is nonsingular and has unit diagonal, while \(H_j\) is monomial and assigns source \(j\) to equation \(x\). Direct multiplication gives
\[
 Q_j^{-1}H_j=W_j^{-1}\Pi_j^{-1}D_jD_j^{-1}\Pi_j=T_j,
 \qquad
 [Q_j^{-1}H_j]_{\mathsf O,:}=C. \tag{21}
\]
Thus the observed vector generated from \(\varepsilon\) has law \(P_X\). The anchor source assumptions and the nonzero, pairwise nonproportional columns of \(C\) show that \((n,C,\varepsilon)\in\mathfrak I(P_X)\), so (20)--(21) meet the observational-law and irreducibility clauses of \(\mathfrak F_x(P_X)\).

It remains to check the intervention boundary rather than infer it from observational solvability. Since row \(j\) was assigned to equation \(x\),
\[
 (Q_j^{-1})_{\mathsf O,x}
 =(T_j)_{\mathsf O,j}(D_j)_{xx}
 =C_{:,j}(D_j)_{xx}. \tag{22}
\]
Both \(C_{xj}\) and \((D_j)_{xx}\) are nonzero, so \((Q_j^{-1})_{xx}\ne0\). The principal cofactor identity then yields \(\det((Q_j)_{-x,-x})\ne0\). Thus \(\mathcal M_j=(n,Q_j,H_j,\varepsilon)\in\mathfrak F_x(P_X)\), and division of (22) by its \(x\)-coordinate proves the displayed vector response. If \(C\) is rational, Gaussian elimination can choose rational extension rows; inversion, the shear, row permutation, and division by nonzero diagonal entries preserve rationality, proving the final assertion.

added_lemmas.statement: Let \((C,\lambda)\) and \((C',\lambda')\) be two normalized numerical factor pairs satisfying all cumulant-magnitude, probe-orientation, lifted-rank, pencil-gap, and dimensional restrictions in the definition of \(\mathfrak P_{p,n,r}(a,\delta,\sigma,\kappa,\Lambda,M)\), and let \(\mathcal T_r=\sum_j\lambda_jc_j^{\otimes r}\) and \(\mathcal T'_r=\sum_j\lambda'_j(c'_j)^{\otimes r}\). If \(\lVert\mathcal T'_r-\mathcal T_r\rVert_F<\epsilon_0\), then a permutation \(\pi\) exists such that \(\lVert C'_{\pi}-C\rVert_F\le L_C\lVert\mathcal T'_r-\mathcal T_r\rVert_F\). Thus the local inverse bound applies to the numerical feasible set of the minimum-distance fit, without requiring the fitted factors to be accompanied by a source law.
added_lemmas.proof_tex:
Put \(e=\lVert\mathcal T'_r-\mathcal T_r\rVert_F\). Contract the last \(q\) modes against \(u^{\otimes(q-1)}\otimes w\), matricize the remaining modes in two blocks of degree \(d\), and denote the resulting matrices by \(M_w,M'_w\). Contraction by unit vectors, matricization, and orthogonal compression do not increase Frobenius norm, so every compressed difference below has operator norm at most \(e\).

Let \(U\) be an orthonormal basis for \(\operatorname{range}(V_d)\), and set
\[
 S=U^\top V_d,
 \qquad A_w=U^\top M_wU
 =S\operatorname{diag}\!\left(\lambda_j(u^\top c_j)^{q-1}(w^\top c_j)\right)S^\top. \tag{23}
\]
The lifted-rank margin gives \(s_{\min}(S)=s_{\min}(V_d)\ge\sigma\), while \(\lVert S\rVert\le\lVert V_d\rVert_F=\sqrt n\). For \(w=u\), every diagonal magnitude in (23) is at least \(\kappa\sigma^q\). Hence
\[
 s_{\min}(A_u)\ge\kappa\sigma^q s_{\min}(S)^2
 \ge\kappa\sigma^{q+2}=\eta,
 \qquad \lVert A_u^{-1}\rVert\le\eta^{-1}. \tag{24}
\]
The same factorization also gives \(\lVert A_w\rVert\le n\Lambda\) for every unit \(w\).

Compress the primed contractions using this same \(U\), so \(A'_w=U^\top M'_wU\) and \(\lVert A'_w-A_w\rVert\le e\). Since \(e<\eta/2\), (24) and the Neumann series imply
\[
 \lVert(A'_u)^{-1}\rVert\le2\eta^{-1}. \tag{25}
\]
Writing \(S'=U^\top V'_d\), the factorization \(A'_u=S'D'_u(S')^\top\), with nonsingular diagonal \(D'_u\), and invertibility of \(A'_u\) show that \(S'\) is invertible. Therefore, for \(G_w=A_wA_u^{-1}\) and \(G'_w=A'_w(A'_u)^{-1}\),
\[
 G_w=S\operatorname{diag}\!\left(\frac{w^\top c_j}{u^\top c_j}\right)S^{-1},
 \quad
 G'_w=S'\operatorname{diag}\!\left(\frac{w^\top c'_j}{u^\top c'_j}\right)(S')^{-1}. \tag{26}
\]
The inverse identity and (24)--(25) give
\[
 \lVert G'_w-G_w\rVert
 \le\left(\frac{2}{\eta}+\frac{2n\Lambda}{\eta^2}\right)e
 =he. \tag{27}
\]

For \(w=v\), the eigenvalues of \(G_v\) are real and pairwise separated by at least \(\sigma\). Around each eigenvalue draw a complex circle of radius \(g=\sigma/3\). From (26), the resolvent on a circle is bounded by \(\chi/g\), where \(\chi=\lVert S\rVert\lVert S^{-1}\rVert\le\sqrt n/\sigma\). The condition \(e<\sigma/(6\chi h)\) makes \((\chi/g)he<1/2\). The resolvent identity and Neumann series therefore show that every circle contains exactly one eigenvalue of \(G'_v\), counted algebraically, and that the corresponding rank-one spectral projectors satisfy
\[
 \lVert P'_j-P_j\rVert
 \le \frac{2\chi^2he}{g}
 =\frac{6\chi^2he}{\sigma},
 \qquad
 \lVert P_j\rVert\le\chi,
 \qquad
 \lVert P'_j\rVert\le2\chi. \tag{28}
\]
Indeed, integrate \((zI-G'_v)^{-1}(G'_v-G_v)(zI-G_v)^{-1}\) around the circle; its length divided by \(2\pi\) is \(g\), which gives (28). Continuity along \(G_v+t(G'_v-G_v)\) and the integer-valued rank of a projector justify the one-eigenvalue pairing. This supplies one common permutation \(\pi\).

For each coordinate vector \(e_i\), define \(z_{ij}=\operatorname{tr}(G_{e_i}P_j)\) and define \(z'_{i,\pi(j)}\) analogously. Simultaneous diagonalization in (26) gives
\[
 z_j=\frac{c_j}{u^\top c_j},
 \qquad
 z'_{\pi(j)}=\frac{c'_{\pi(j)}}{u^\top c'_{\pi(j)}}. \tag{29}
\]
Using \(|\operatorname{tr}(R)|\le n\lVert R\rVert\), \(\lVert G_{e_i}\rVert\le n\Lambda/\eta\), and (27)--(28), we obtain coordinatewise
\[
 |z'_{i,\pi(j)}-z_{ij}|
 \le nh\left(2\chi+\frac{6n\Lambda\chi^2}{\eta\sigma}\right)e
 =L_ze. \tag{30}
\]
The probe orientation fixes the sign in (29), and unit normalization gives \(\lVert z_j\rVert=1/(u^\top c_j)\ge1\), with the same statement for \(z'_{\pi(j)}\). Normalization on vectors of norm at least one is two-Lipschitz, so (30) yields
\[
 \lVert c'_{\pi(j)}-c_j\rVert_2
 \le2\sqrt p\,L_ze. \tag{31}
\]
Squaring (31), summing over \(j\), and taking square roots proves
\[
 \lVert C'_{\pi}-C\rVert_F
 \le2\sqrt{np}\,L_ze=L_Ce.
\]
Only the displayed numerical restrictions were used, which proves the extension to the estimator's feasible factor set.

proposed_statement_changes.current: Under the population assumptions, \(J_x(C)\ne\varnothing\) and the sharp equilibrium-effect set over the entire source-minimal fixed-law fiber is \[\{\theta_{y\leftarrow x}(\mathcal M):\mathcal M\in\mathfrak F_x(C,\varepsilon)\}=\mathcal R_{xy}(C)=\{C_{yj}/C_{xj}:C_{xj}\ne0,\ \operatorname{rank}(C_{-x,-j})=p-1\}.\] All values and one exact witness per value are certifiable in \(O(n^4)\) arithmetic operations.
proposed_statement_changes.proposed:
Under the population assumptions, the full observational-law fiber \(\mathfrak F_x(P_X)\) is nonempty, every one of its completions has source count \(n\), and
\[
 \{\boldsymbol\theta_{-x\leftarrow x}(\mathcal M):\mathcal M\in\mathfrak F_x(P_X)\}
 =\mathcal R_x^{\mathrm{vec}}(C)
 =\left\{\frac{C_{-x,j}}{C_{xj}}:C_{xj}\ne0,\ \operatorname{rank}(C_{-x,-j})=p-1\right\}.
\]
For every \(y\ne x\), coordinate projection gives
\[
 \{\theta_{y\leftarrow x}(\mathcal M):\mathcal M\in\mathfrak F_x(P_X)\}
 =\mathcal R_{xy}(C).
\]
Every alternative observed mixing matrix in the fiber equals \(C\Pi D\) for a permutation \(\Pi\) and nonsingular diagonal \(D\), so the displayed frontiers are functionals of \(P_X\) on the irreducible class. The algorithm \(\operatorname{Cert}(C,x)\) returns one exact same-law completion for every \(j\in J_x(C)\), and all values and witnesses are certifiable in \(O(n^4)\) real-arithmetic operations.
proposed_statement_changes.reason: The directive strengthens the estimand from the fixed representation to the full irreducible observational-law fiber and from one scalar coordinate to the whole one-intervention response vector. The published irreducible-ICA uniqueness theorem makes the stronger law-level claim true, while the existing witnesses supply sharpness.

proposed_statement_changes.current: The effect \(\theta_{y\leftarrow x}\) is identified over \(\mathfrak F_x(C,\varepsilon)\) if and only if \( |\mathcal R_{xy}(C)|=1\), equivalently \(\operatorname{rank}(C_{\{x,y\},J_x(C)})=1\). If this condition fails, \(\operatorname{Cert}(C,x)\) returns two same-law completions with distinct effects in \(O(n^3)\) additional arithmetic operations after the shared basis inverse.
proposed_statement_changes.proposed: The full one-intervention response vector \(\boldsymbol\theta_{-x\leftarrow x}\) is identified over \(\mathfrak F_x(P_X)\) if and only if \(|J_x(C)|=1\), equivalently \(|\mathcal R_x^{\mathrm{vec}}(C)|=1\). For each \(y\ne x\), the scalar response \(\theta_{y\leftarrow x}\) is identified if and only if \(|\mathcal R_{xy}(C)|=1\), equivalently \(\operatorname{rank}(C_{\{x,y\},J_x(C)})=1\). If vector identification fails, \(\operatorname{Cert}(C,x)\) returns two same-law completions with distinct entire response vectors; if the scalar rank condition fails, it returns two with distinct \(y\)-responses. Either pair costs \(O(n^3)\) additional arithmetic operations after the shared basis inverse.
proposed_statement_changes.reason: The response-vector promotion requires its own exact point-identification test. Pairwise nonproportional columns make the vector map injective on the admissible-source set, while the original two-row rank test remains the correct criterion for each scalar projection.

proposed_statement_changes.current: For every \(N\) and every nonempty class \(\mathfrak P_{p,n,r}(a,\delta,\sigma,\kappa,\Lambda,M)\) with \(d\ge1\), \(q\ge1\), and \(n\le\binom{p+d-1}{d}\), the iid confidence unions satisfy \[\inf_{\zeta=(P_X,C,\varepsilon,\lambda)\in\mathfrak P_{p,n,r}}P_X^{\otimes N}\!\left\{\begin{array}{l}\mathcal R_{xy}(C)\subseteq\mathcal U_{xy}\text{ for every }x\ne y\in\mathsf O,\\ \text{and, if }2\tau_N<\epsilon_0\text{ and }b_N<\min\{a,\delta\}/2,\text{ then after one common permutation}\\ \widehat J_x=J_x(C)\text{ and }d_H(\mathcal U_{xy},\mathcal R_{xy}(C))\le2w_N\text{ for every }x\ne y\in\mathsf O\end{array}\right\}\ge1-\alpha.\] Uniformly over the same representation-indexed tuples in the informative regime, \(2w_N=O(N^{-1/2})\).
proposed_statement_changes.proposed:
For every \(N\) and every nonempty class \(\mathfrak P_{p,n,r}(a,\delta,\sigma,\kappa,\Lambda,M)\) with \(d\ge1\), \(q\ge1\), and \(n\le\binom{p+d-1}{d}\), the iid scalar and response-vector confidence unions satisfy
\[
\inf_{\zeta=(P_X,C,\varepsilon,\lambda)\in\mathfrak P_{p,n,r}}
P_X^{\otimes N}\!\left\{
\begin{array}{l}
\mathcal R_x^{\mathrm{vec}}(C)\subseteq\mathcal U_x^{\mathrm{vec}}
\text{ and }\mathcal R_{xy}(C)\subseteq\mathcal U_{xy}
\text{ for every }x\ne y\in\mathsf O,\\
\text{and, if }2\tau_N<\epsilon_0\text{ and }b_N<\min\{a,\delta\}/2,
\text{ then after one common permutation}\\
\widehat J_x=J_x(C),\quad
d_H(\mathcal U_x^{\mathrm{vec}},\mathcal R_x^{\mathrm{vec}}(C))\le2w_N^{\mathrm{vec}},\quad
d_H(\mathcal U_{xy},\mathcal R_{xy}(C))\le2w_N
\text{ for every }x\ne y
\end{array}\right\}\ge1-\alpha.
\]
By the sharp-frontier theorem these are confidence unions for the full observational-law-fiber causal targets. Uniformly over the same representation-indexed tuples in the informative regime, \(2w_N^{\mathrm{vec}}=O(N^{-1/2})\) and \(2w_N=O(N^{-1/2})\).
proposed_statement_changes.reason: The confidence object must preserve cross-outcome dependence by using source-indexed Euclidean balls for entire response vectors. The scalar intervals remain valid coordinate projections, and the same tensor event yields both simultaneous bounds.

proposed_statement_changes.current: For a fixed normalized representation \(X=C\varepsilon\) with mutually independent, nondegenerate, moment-determinate non-Gaussian sources and pairwise nonproportional mixing columns, set \(m_{\mathrm V}=n-1\) and \(R_0=3m_{\mathrm V}\). There is an exact population inverse which, for each cumulant order \(\nu\ge R_0\), reshapes \(\operatorname{cum}_\nu(X)\) with block degrees at least \(m_{\mathrm V}\), takes its unique minimal three-factor decomposition, and unions the recovered projective directions. It stops after a finite representation-dependent order and recovers \(\{[c_1],\ldots,[c_n]\}\), hence every \(\mathcal R_{xy}(C)\), without cross-order label alignment. No finite stopping order is uniform over the stated moment-determinate class. Already for \(p=n=2\), that class admits two fixed, separated direction sets and associated sequences of observational experiments whose \(N\)-sample total-variation distance tends to zero. Consequently no inverse is uniformly consistent there, and no confidence procedure with coverage strictly greater than one half can have uniformly vanishing Hausdorff uncertainty, so a uniform root-\(N\) heterogeneous-order frontier law does not follow without quantitative non-Gaussianity, moment, Veronese-conditioning, angular, probe/eigen-gap, deletion-rank, and denominator margins. The existing common-order separated theorem retains its simultaneous coverage and root-\(N\) conclusion.

proposed.statement:
Under the population assumptions, the full observational-law fiber \(\mathfrak F_x(P_X)\) is nonempty, every one of its completions has source count \(n\), and
\[
 \{\boldsymbol\theta_{-x\leftarrow x}(\mathcal M):\mathcal M\in\mathfrak F_x(P_X)\}
 =\mathcal R_x^{\mathrm{vec}}(C)
 =\left\{\frac{C_{-x,j}}{C_{xj}}:C_{xj}\ne0,\ \operatorname{rank}(C_{-x,-j})=p-1\right\}.
\]
For every \(y\ne x\), coordinate projection gives
\[
 \{\theta_{y\leftarrow x}(\mathcal M):\mathcal M\in\mathfrak F_x(P_X)\}
 =\mathcal R_{xy}(C).
\]
Every alternative observed mixing matrix in the fiber equals \(C\Pi D\) for a permutation \(\Pi\) and nonsingular diagonal \(D\), so the displayed frontiers are functionals of \(P_X\) on the irreducible class. The algorithm \(\operatorname{Cert}(C,x)\) returns one exact same-law completion for every \(j\in J_x(C)\), and all values and witnesses are certifiable in \(O(n^4)\) real-arithmetic operations.

prose_updates.tldr: For an irreducible all-non-Gaussian observed law, every source-minimal cyclic one-shock-per-equation completion has the same source directions up to permutation and scaling. Its sharp response to one hard intervention is therefore the finite vector set \(\mathcal R_x^{\mathrm{vec}}(C)=\{C_{-x,j}/C_{xj}:j\in J_x(C)\}\); scalar effects are coordinate projections of these same vectors. One latent-row shear and one perfect matching construct every same-law witness in \(O(n^4)\) total arithmetic operations. A separated common-order iid class admits simultaneous scalar intervals and source-indexed Euclidean response balls with uniform coverage and root-\(N\) Hausdorff uncertainty. Without a common active cumulant order, exact population recovery starts at order \(2n-1\), obeys the adaptive elbow \(2R_\nu-1\), and stops at a finite model-specific order, but no uniform finite order or uniform inference rate exists under qualitative moment determinacy alone.

project_justification.gap: Published all-non-Gaussian ICA theory identifies the source count and directions from the full observed law, and published latent cyclic LiNG work characterizes graph-level distributional equivalence. Neither computes the exact hard-intervention response-vector image of every irreducible, source-minimal, postintervention-solvable completion entailing one observed law.
project_justification.niche: Law-level ICA uniqueness reduces every alternative completion to a permutation and scaling of one recovered direction matrix. The deletion-rank map is invariant under those indeterminacies and preserves all outcomes attached to the same source, so the causal query can be solved without graph enumeration or dynamical stability.
project_justification.fill: The note proves the sharp response-vector and scalar frontiers over the full irreducible observational-law fiber, constructs all witnesses and exact countermodels, characterizes vector and coordinatewise point identification, gives an \(O(n^4)\) certificate, establishes simultaneous scalar/vector iid confidence unions, and derives the adaptive heterogeneous-order population inverse and its uniform-impossibility boundary.

sampling_model.design: Observational iid sampling under \(P_X^{\otimes N}\) for each separated representation-indexed tuple \(\zeta=(P_X,C,\varepsilon,\lambda)\). The causal estimand ranges over the full irreducible observational-law fiber; published ICA uniqueness proves that its deletion-rank frontier is invariant to the chosen normalized representation.
sampling_model.units: \(N\) independent copies of \(X=C\varepsilon\) under \(P_X^{\otimes N}\), indexed by one tuple \(\zeta\in\mathfrak P_{p,n,r}(a,\delta,\sigma,\kappa,\Lambda,M)\).
sampling_model.treatment: A single hard intervention replaces the structural equation for observed coordinate \(x\) by \(V_x=t\); the target is the joint equilibrium response of all other observed coordinates. This is not a claim about simultaneous interventions on several treatment coordinates.
sampling_model.overlap: Not applicable; the relevant regularity conditions are the treatment-loading, deletion-singular-value, lifted-rank, cumulant, and pencil-separation margins.
sampling_model.nuisance_estimation: Normalized mixing directions are recovered by the common-order cumulant tensor pencil and a separated minimum-distance fit. One common source permutation aligns the whole response vector; no outcome-wise relabeling is permitted.

Those are published law-level inputs here; the new step is to prove that deletion ranks, response ratios, and the entire hard-intervention frontier are invariant under the permitted monomial change and that every point has a postintervention-solvable structural witness. prose_updates.interpretation: A point of \(\mathcal R_x^{\mathrm{vec}}(C)\) is one jointly attainable equilibrium response vector from a single structural completion. Its coordinates may be reported as scalar frontiers, but values from different source indices cannot be combined into a fictitious cross-outcome vector. Pairwise nonproportional directions imply that the whole response vector is point identified exactly when one source passes the deletion-rank test; an individual outcome may still be point identified when several admissible sources share that one slope. For the fourteen-stock HSI example, the method would attach at most one vector per recovered source direction to a chosen stock intervention and can return two exact models when those vectors differ. No numerical HSI effect or confidence ball is asserted here.
prose_updates.technical_internal_limitation: The observational-law enlargement is limited to irreducible ICA representations and source-minimal LiNG completions with one independent shock per equation. Reducible representations, zero or duplicated/proportional directions, shock splitting or merging, and merely graphical irreducibility without this source-minimal representation condition are excluded because the published ICA uniqueness theorem does not identify those fibers and the frontier can change. The \(O(n^4)\) certificate uses exact real arithmetic after \(C\) is available and is not a bit-complexity or floating-point guarantee. Common-order inference assumes fixed moment, tensor-rank, pencil-gap, deletion-rank, and denominator margins; the constrained fit is specified statistically but no polynomial-time global optimizer is claimed. The HSI daily series is dependent and may exhibit mechanism changes, so it supports only a population illustration unless a time-series concentration theorem and an informative empirical separation certificate are supplied.
prose_updates.honest_scope: The population theorem covers the full observational-law fiber of irreducible, source-minimal, one-shock-per-equation cyclic LiNG completions satisfying observational and specified-treatment postintervention solvability, with no stability restriction. It returns the full response to one intervention and all scalar coordinate projections, not a Cartesian product and not a joint multiple-intervention effect. Published all-non-Gaussian ICA uniqueness is an input, not a contribution. The new population inverse for heterogeneous source-specific cumulant orders is exact and stops after a finite model-specific order, beginning universally at \(2n-1\) and at the adaptive elbow \(2R_\nu-1\) for an active rank \(R_\nu\); only a uniform stopping order and uniform inference over the qualitative class are impossible. Uniform root-\(N\) confidence claims are restricted to the declared common-order separated iid class. Stability-refined fibers, reducible or split-source completions, unknown source count, data-selected probes without a new uniform argument, dependent-time-series HSI inference, and favorable empirical constants remain outside scope.
