semantic_closure.proof_tex:
It suffices to prove independence for an arbitrary subcollection \(z_1,\ldots,z_k\), where \(1\le k\le R\). For each ordered pair \(i
e j\), nonproportionality supplies a linear functional \(\ell_{ij}\) such that \(\ell_{ij}(z_j)=0\) and \(\ell_{ij}(z_i)
e0\): take a functional vanishing on the line spanned by \(z_j\) but not on \(z_i\). Choose also a linear functional \(g_i\) with \(g_i(z_i)
e0\). The homogeneous polynomial
\[
 f_i(z)=g_i(z)^{s-k+1}\prod_{j
e i}\ell_{ij}(z)
\]
has degree \(s\), is nonzero at \(z_i\), and vanishes at every \(z_j\) with \(j
e i\). Every homogeneous polynomial of degree \(s\) is a linear functional on the symmetric tensor power, so there is \(L_i\) with \(L_i(z^{\otimes s})=f_i(z)\). semantic_closure.statement: For every integer \(K\ge3\) and every \(\rho>0\), there exists a centered, variance-one, non-Gaussian, moment-determinate probability law \(F\) on \(\mathbb R\) such that \(d_{\mathrm{TV}}(F,\mathcal N(0,1))<\rho\) and the first \(K\) raw moments, hence the cumulants through order \(K\), agree with those of \(\mathcal N(0,1)\).
semantic_closure.proof_tex:
Let \(\phi\) be the standard Gaussian density. Choose \(K+2\) pairwise disjoint bounded intervals \(I_0,\ldots,I_{K+1}\), each of positive Gaussian probability. The \((K+1)\)-by-\((K+2)\) matrix
\[
 A_{r\ell}=\int_{I_\ell}x^r\phi(x)\,dx,
 \qquad 0\le r\le K,
\]
has a nonzero null vector \(b=(b_0,\ldots,b_{K+1})\). Rescale it so that \(\max_\ell|b_\ell|=1\), and define the bounded, nonzero function \(h=\sum_\ell b_\ell\mathbf 1_{I_\ell}\). Then
\[
 \int x^rh(x)\phi(x)\,dx=0,
 \qquad 0\le r\le K. \tag{22}
\]
For \(0<t<1\), set \(f_t(x)=\phi(x)(1+th(x))\). The case \(r=0\) of (22) makes \(f_t\) integrate to one, and \(|h|\le1\) makes it strictly positive. Since \(h\) is nonzero on a set of positive Gaussian measure, \(f_t\ne\phi\). Equation (22) says that its first \(K\) moments, including mean zero and variance one, equal the Gaussian moments. Cumulants through order \(K\) are universal polynomials in the moments through the same order, so they also agree.

Moreover \(f_t\le2\phi\), whence its even moments satisfy \(m_{2s}(f_t)\le2(2s-1)!!\). It follows that \(m_{2s}(f_t)^{-1/(2s)}\) is bounded below by a positive constant times \(s^{-1/2}\), and therefore the Carleman series diverges. The cited Carleman criterion makes \(F_t\) moment determinate. Finally,
\[
 d_{\mathrm{TV}}(F_t,\mathcal N(0,1))
 =\frac t2\int|h(x)|\phi(x)\,dx\longrightarrow0
\]
as \(t\downarrow0\). Choosing \(t\) small enough proves the claim.

carrier.proof_tex:
For every order \(\nu\), write \(\lambda_{j,\nu}=\operatorname{cum}_\nu(\varepsilon_j)\). Moment determinacy presupposes finite moments of every order. Mutual independence makes mixed source cumulants vanish, while multilinearity of cumulants gives the observable tensor
\[
 \mathcal T_\nu=\operatorname{cum}_\nu(X)
 =\sum_{j=1}^n\lambda_{j,\nu}c_j^{\otimes\nu}. \tag{50}
\]
Let \(A_\nu=\{j:\lambda_{j,\nu}\ne0\}\) and \(R_\nu=|A_\nu|\). Suppose first that \(R_\nu\ge2\) and \(\nu\ge2R_\nu-1\). Put
\[
 \ell_1=\ell_2=R_\nu-1,
 \qquad
 \ell_3=\nu-2R_\nu+2\ge1. \tag{51}
\]
Reshaping (50) into these three blocks yields
\[
 \widetilde{\mathcal T}_\nu
 =\sum_{j\in A_\nu}\lambda_{j,\nu}
 \operatorname{vec}(c_j^{\otimes\ell_1})\otimes
 \operatorname{vec}(c_j^{\otimes\ell_2})\otimes
 \operatorname{vec}(c_j^{\otimes\ell_3}). \tag{52}
\]
The Veronese--Lagrange rank lemma applies to each of the first two factors because \(\ell_1=\ell_2=R_\nu-1\); their Kruskal ranks equal \(R_\nu\). Any two columns of the third factor are linearly independent: applying the same lemma to that pair uses only \(\ell_3\ge1\). Hence its Kruskal rank is at least two. Therefore
\[
 k_1+k_2+k_3\ge R_\nu+R_\nu+2=2R_\nu+2. \tag{53}
\]
The established Kruskal three-factor uniqueness lemma applied to (52) proves essential uniqueness up to a common permutation and reciprocal nonzero scalings. The tensor rank is exactly \(R_\nu\): the first factor matrix has full column rank, and the Khatri--Rao product of the second and third factors has full column rank. For the latter claim, apply a left-inverse row selecting one column of the second factor to a linear dependence among the Khatri--Rao columns; the selected nonzero third-factor column forces that coefficient to vanish, and repeat for every column. Thus the mode-one matricization has rank \(R_\nu\), furnishing the matching lower bound on tensor rank. If \(R_\nu=1\), a nonzero tensor in (50) is rank one and its common projective preimage is immediate; if \(R_\nu=0\), the tensor is zero and contributes no direction. This proves the adaptive elbow \(\nu\ge2R_\nu-1\).

For a recovery rule that knows \(n\) but not \(R_\nu\), take any \(\nu\ge2n-1\) and use the fixed degrees
\[
 (\ell_1,\ell_2,\ell_3)=(n-1,n-1,\nu-2n+2). \tag{54}
\]
For every active rank \(R_\nu\le n\), the first two degrees are at least \(R_\nu-1\), while the third is at least one. The argument (52)--(53) therefore applies unchanged. A computable exact population operation is the following constrained decomposition: minimize \(R\in\{0,\ldots,n\}\) over nonzero coefficients \(\gamma_1,\ldots,\gamma_R\), nonzero vectors \(z_1,\ldots,z_R\in\mathbb R^p\), and block factors \(b_{s\ell}\), subject to
\[
 \widetilde{\mathcal T}_\nu
 =\sum_{\ell=1}^R\gamma_\ell b_{1\ell}\otimes b_{2\ell}\otimes b_{3\ell},
 \qquad
 b_{s\ell}=\operatorname{vec}(z_\ell^{\otimes\ell_s})
 \quad(s=1,2,3). \tag{55}
\]
Equations (52)--(54), minimality, and Kruskal uniqueness prove that the solutions of (55) return exactly \(\{[c_j]:j\in A_\nu\}\). The Veronese map has no extra real projective collision: if \(z^{\otimes s}\) and \(w^{\otimes s}\) are proportional for \(s\ge1\) while \(z,w\) are not, choose a linear functional vanishing on \(w\) but not on \(z\) and contract all \(s\) modes, a contradiction.

By the established Marcinkiewicz cumulant-tail lemma, each nondegenerate non-Gaussian source with all moments has infinitely many nonzero cumulants of order at least three. Consequently, for every source \(j\), there is some \(\nu_j\ge2n-1\) with \(\lambda_{j,\nu_j}\ne0\). Since there are finitely many sources,
\[
 K_{C,\varepsilon}=\max_{1\le j\le n}\nu_j<\infty. \tag{56}
\]
Starting at \(2n-1\), solve (55) and take the set-theoretic union of its recovered projective directions. Pairwise nonproportionality prevents merging, and the rule stops when the union reaches its known cardinality \(n\), no later than (56). Labels need not be transported across orders. \[

\[

\]

\[

target_declaration.statement: For a fixed normalized representation \(X=C\varepsilon\) with mutually independent, nondegenerate, moment-determinate non-Gaussian sources and pairwise nonproportional mixing columns, set \(m_{\mathrm V}=n-1\) and \(R_0=3m_{\mathrm V}\). There is an exact population inverse which, for each cumulant order \(\nu\ge R_0\), reshapes \(\operatorname{cum}_\nu(X)\) with block degrees at least \(m_{\mathrm V}\), takes its unique minimal three-factor decomposition, and unions the recovered projective directions. It stops after a finite representation-dependent order and recovers \(\{[c_1],\ldots,[c_n]\}\), hence every \(\mathcal R_{xy}(C)\), without cross-order label alignment. No finite stopping order is uniform over the stated moment-determinate class. Already for \(p=n=2\), that class admits two fixed, separated direction sets and associated sequences of observational experiments whose \(N\)-sample total-variation distance tends to zero. Consequently no inverse is uniformly consistent there, and no confidence procedure with coverage strictly greater than one half can have uniformly vanishing Hausdorff uncertainty, so a uniform root-\(N\) heterogeneous-order frontier law does not follow without quantitative non-Gaussianity, moment, Veronese-conditioning, angular, probe/eigen-gap, deletion-rank, and denominator margins. The existing common-order separated theorem retains its simultaneous coverage and root-\(N\) conclusion.
target_declaration.proof_tex:
Write \(\lambda_{j,\nu}=\operatorname{cum}_\nu(\varepsilon_j)\). Mutual independence implies additivity of the log characteristic function:
\[
 \log\mathbb E\exp(i t^{\top}X)
 =\sum_{j=1}^n\log\mathbb E\exp\{i(t^{\top}c_j)\varepsilon_j\}.
\]
Equating the formal derivatives of total order \(\nu\), which exist because the moment sequences exist, gives the observable cumulant tensor
\[
 \mathcal T_\nu=\operatorname{cum}_\nu(X)
 =\sum_{j=1}^n\lambda_{j,\nu}c_j^{\otimes \nu}. \tag{23}
\]
Set \(m_{\mathrm V}=n-1\). For \(\nu\ge R_0=3m_{\mathrm V}\), take \(\ell_1=\ell_2=m_{\mathrm V}\) and \(\ell_3=\nu-2m_{\mathrm V}\), so \(\ell_1,\ell_2,\ell_3\ge m_{\mathrm V}\). Let \(A_\nu=\{j:\lambda_{j,\nu}\ne0\}\) and \(R_\nu=|A_\nu|\). Reshaping (23) into three blocks yields
\[
 \widetilde{\mathcal T}_\nu
 =\sum_{j\in A_\nu}\lambda_{j,\nu}
 \operatorname{vec}(c_j^{\otimes \ell_1})\otimes
 \operatorname{vec}(c_j^{\otimes \ell_2})\otimes
 \operatorname{vec}(c_j^{\otimes \ell_3}). \tag{24}
\]
If \(R_\nu=0\), the tensor is zero and contributes no direction. If \(R_\nu\ge1\), the Veronese--Lagrange lemma applies because each block degree is at least \(n-1\ge R_\nu-1\). Thus each of the three factor matrices in (24) has Kruskal rank \(R_\nu\). For \(R_\nu\ge2\),
\[
 k_{\ell_1}+k_{\ell_2}+k_{\ell_3}=3R_\nu\ge2R_\nu+2,
\]
so Kruskal's cited Theorem 4a makes (24) essentially unique, up to one common permutation and reciprocal component scalings. The case \(R_\nu=1\) is immediate. The decomposition has minimal rank \(R_\nu\): its mode-one matricization has rank \(R_\nu\), since the first factor matrix has full column rank and the Khatri--Rao product of the other two factor matrices has full column rank. For the latter assertion, applying a left-inverse row for one column of the second factor matrix to a putative linear dependence isolates a nonzero third-factor column and forces that coefficient to vanish.

This gives an explicit population recovery operation at order \(\nu\): minimize \(R\) over integers \(0\le R\le n\) and variables \(\gamma_1,\ldots,\gamma_R\ne0\) and nonzero block factors \(z_{s\ell}\), subject to
\[
 \widetilde{\mathcal T}_\nu=\sum_{\ell=1}^R\gamma_\ell z_{1\ell}\otimes z_{2\ell}\otimes z_{3\ell},
 \qquad z_{1\ell}\in\{\operatorname{vec}(z^{\otimes \ell_1}):z\ne0\},
\]
with the analogous Veronese constraints of degrees \(\ell_2\) and \(\ell_3\) on \(z_{2\ell}\) and \(z_{3\ell}\), and with the three factors in each summand required to have a common projective preimage. The preceding rank and uniqueness argument proves that its solution set is exactly the active directions in (24), modulo permutation and component scalings. The Veronese map is injective on real projective space: if \(z^{\otimes \ell_1}\) and \(w^{\otimes \ell_1}\) are proportional while \(z,w\) are not, a linear functional vanishing at \(w\) but not at \(z\), contracted in all \(\ell_1\) modes, gives a contradiction. Hence every active \([c_j]\) is computable from the exact tensor.

By the cited Marcinkiewicz cumulant theorem, every nondegenerate non-Gaussian source with moments of all orders has infinitely many nonzero cumulants. Therefore, for each \(j\), some \(\nu_j\ge R_0\) has \(\lambda_{j,\nu_j}\ne0\). Since there are only \(n\) sources,
\[
 K_{C,\varepsilon}=\max_{1\le j\le n}\nu_j<\infty. \tag{25}
\]
Incrementing \(\nu\) from \(R_0\), decomposing (24), and taking the set-theoretic union of the recovered projective directions stops as soon as the union has its known size \(n\), no later than (25). Pairwise nonproportionality prevents accidental merging. No labels need be transported between orders. Column ratios and deletion ranks are invariant under nonzero rescaling and permutation, so applying the deletion-rank map to these projective directions recovers every \(\mathcal R_{xy}(C)\).

We next prove that the stopping order and inference conclusion cannot be uniform under the frozen qualitative assumptions. Fix any finite \(K\ge3\). The near-Gaussian moment-matching lemma supplies a non-Gaussian moment-determinate law \(F\) whose first \(K\) moments equal those of \(\mathcal N(0,1)\). Let two independent sources have law \(F\), and consider
\[

 \qquad
 C_1=\begin{pmatrix}\cos\gamma&-\sin\gamma\\[2pt]\sin\gamma&\cos\gamma\end{pmatrix},
 \qquad 0<\gamma<\pi/4. \tag{26}
\]
Both matrices have normalized, nonzero, nonproportional columns. Independence and equality of the univariate moments through \(K\) imply that all joint source moments through total degree \(K\) are Gaussian. Orthogonal invariance of the Gaussian moments then shows that the two observed models in (26) have identical moments, and hence identical cumulant tensors, through order \(K\), although their projective direction sets are separated by angle \(\gamma\). No inverse using a uniformly fixed finite order can distinguish them.

For the statistical obstruction, use the same bounded perturbation construction with laws \(F_t\) satisfying \(d_{\mathrm{TV}}(F_t,\mathcal N(0,1))\to0\). \]
Choose \(t=t_N\) so that the right side is at most \(N^{-2}\). The product inequality gives

\]

\[

 \ge1-d_{\mathrm{TV}}(P_{0,t_N}^{\otimes N},P_{1,t_N}^{\otimes N}),
\]
which tends to one by (28), a contradiction.

The causal frontiers are separated as well. For \(x=1,y=2\), direct evaluation of the deletion minors gives
\[
 \mathcal R_{12}(C_0)=\{0\},
 \qquad
 \mathcal R_{12}(C_1)=\{\tan\gamma,-\cot\gamma\}. \tag{29}
\]
Thus the same testing argument rules out uniform Hausdorff consistency for the frontier. More generally, suppose a random confidence region for the frontier has uniform coverage \(1-\alpha>1/2\) and uniformly vanishing Hausdorff diameter. By (28), under the first experiment it contains the first frontier with probability at least \(1-\alpha\) and the second with probability at least \(1-\alpha-o(1)\). Their intersection has probability at least \(1-2\alpha-o(1)>0\), but on that intersection its diameter is at least the fixed Hausdorff separation in (29), a contradiction.

Two deterministic boundary sequences show why the causal map additionally needs denominator and deletion-rank margins. After harmless column normalization, for
\[

\]
the frontier \(\mathcal R_{12}(D_t)=\{1/t,1\}\) for \(t\ne0,1\), whereas \(\mathcal R_{12}(D_0)=\{1\}\). For
\[
 E_0=\begin{pmatrix}1&1&0&1\\1&0&0&0\\0&0&1&1\end{pmatrix}
\]
and \(E_t\) obtained by replacing its \((2,2)\) entry by \(t\ne0\), one checks \(\mathcal R_{12}(E_0)=\{0\}\) but \(\mathcal R_{12}(E_t)=\{0,t,1\}\). All columns are nonzero and pairwise nonproportional near zero, and the matrices have full row rank. Thus qualitative nonvanishing and rank conditions alone do not yield a uniform modulus. Quantitative lower cumulant, moment, Veronese-conditioning, angular, probe/eigen-gap, deletion-rank, and denominator controls are precisely the type of hypotheses needed for a robust finite-order analysis; the frozen common-order separated class supplies them, and the already proved common-order inverse and confidence theorem retain their simultaneous coverage and root-\(N\) Hausdorff conclusion. The heterogeneous population inverse is therefore positive, while heterogeneous uniform inference over the unrestricted class is negative rather than solved.

Then the columns \(z_1^{\otimes s},\ldots,z_R^{\otimes s}\) have Kruskal rank \(R\); equivalently, every subcollection is linearly independent.

It suffices to prove independence for an arbitrary subcollection \(z_1,\ldots,z_k\), where \(1\le k\le R\). For each ordered pair \(i
e j\), nonproportionality supplies a linear functional \(\ell_{ij}\) such that \(\ell_{ij}(z_j)=0\) and \(\ell_{ij}(z_i)
e0\): take a functional vanishing on the line spanned by \(z_j\) but not on \(z_i\). Choose also a linear functional \(g_i\) with \(g_i(z_i)
e0\). The homogeneous polynomial
\[
 f_i(z)=g_i(z)^{s-k+1}\prod_{j
e i}\ell_{ij}(z)
\]
has degree \(s\), is nonzero at \(z_i\), and vanishes at every \(z_j\) with \(j
e i\). Every homogeneous polynomial of degree \(s\) is a linear functional on the symmetric tensor power, so there is \(L_i\) with \(L_i(z^{\otimes s})=f_i(z)\). If \(\sum_{j=1}^k a_jz_j^{\otimes s}=0\), applying \(L_i\) gives \(a_if_i(z_i)=0\), hence \(a_i=0\). This holds for every \(i\), proving independence of the arbitrary subcollection and therefore Kruskal rank \(R\).

Consequently a nondegenerate non-Gaussian variable with moments of every order has infinitely many nonzero cumulants of order at least three.

attestation.note: This is the cumulant-tail consequence of Marcinkiewicz's theorem used by the orchestrator-directed population argument; the DOI is supplied as the stable source handle.

semantic_closure.statement: For every integer \(K\ge3\) and every \(\rho>0\), there exists a centered, variance-one, non-Gaussian, moment-determinate probability law \(F\) on \(\mathbb R\) such that \(d_{\mathrm{TV}}(F,\mathcal N(0,1))<\rho\) and the first \(K\) raw moments, hence the cumulants through order \(K\), agree with those of \(\mathcal N(0,1)\).
semantic_closure.proof_tex:
Let \(\phi\) be the standard Gaussian density. Choose \(K+2\) pairwise disjoint bounded intervals \(I_0,\ldots,I_{K+1}\), each of positive Gaussian probability. The \((K+1)\)-by-\((K+2)\) matrix
\[
 A_{r\ell}=\int_{I_\ell}x^r\phi(x)\,dx,
 \qquad 0\le r\le K,
\]
has a nonzero null vector \(b=(b_0,\ldots,b_{K+1})\). Rescale it so that \(\max_\ell|b_\ell|=1\), and define the bounded, nonzero function \(h=\sum_\ell b_\ell\mathbf 1_{I_\ell}\). Then
\[
 \int x^rh(x)\phi(x)\,dx=0,
 \qquad 0\le r\le K. \tag{22}
\]
For \(0<t<1\), set \(f_t(x)=\phi(x)(1+th(x))\). The case \(r=0\) of (22) makes \(f_t\) integrate to one, and \(|h|\le1\) makes it strictly positive. Since \(h\) is nonzero on a set of positive Gaussian measure, \(f_t\ne\phi\). Equation (22) says that its first \(K\) moments, including mean zero and variance one, equal the Gaussian moments. Cumulants through order \(K\) are universal polynomials in the moments through the same order, so they also agree.

Moreover \(f_t\le2\phi\), whence its even moments satisfy \(m_{2s}(f_t)\le2(2s-1)!!\). It follows that \(m_{2s}(f_t)^{-1/(2s)}\) is bounded below by a positive constant times \(s^{-1/2}\), and therefore the Carleman series diverges. The cited Carleman criterion makes \(F_t\) moment determinate. Finally,
\[
 d_{\mathrm{TV}}(F_t,\mathcal N(0,1))
 =\frac t2\int|h(x)|\phi(x)\,dx\longrightarrow0
\]
as \(t\downarrow0\). Choosing \(t\) small enough proves the claim.

semantic_closure.statement: For two members of \(\mathfrak P_{p,n,r}(a,\delta,\sigma,\kappa,\Lambda,M)\) with cumulant tensors \(\mathcal T_r\) and \(\mathcal T'_r\), if \(\lVert\mathcal T'_r-\mathcal T_r\rVert_F<\epsilon_0\), then a permutation \(\pi\) exists such that \(\lVert C'_{\pi}-C\rVert_F\le L_C\lVert\mathcal T'_r-\mathcal T_r\rVert_F\). The map \(\operatorname{OICAInv}\) recovers the directions attaining this bound.
semantic_closure.justification: An explicit inverse modulus is the bridge from moment uncertainty to uncertainty for a discontinuously selected causal set.
semantic_closure.gap: WangSeigal2026 gives population OICA identifiability and coupled recovery, while AnandkumarGeJanzamin2015 gives component perturbation bounds; neither supplies this local inverse for deletion-rank effect inference.
semantic_closure.consumer: It supplies the numerical certificate needed to distinguish real effect ambiguity from instability of tensor decomposition.
semantic_closure.proof_tex:
All unlabeled matrix norms below are operator two-norms. Let \(\Delta=\lVert\mathcal T'_r-\mathcal T_r\rVert_F<\epsilon_0\). For each probe \(w\in\{u,v,e_1,\ldots,e_p\}\), contraction against unit vectors and orthogonal compression have norm at most one. Consequently, if \(M_w,M'_w\) are the contracted matricizations, then
\[
 \lVert M'_w-M_w\rVert\le\Delta.
\]

Choose an orthonormal basis \(U\) for \(\operatorname{range}(V_d)\), set \(S=U^{\mathsf T}V_d\), and compress both tensors into this same space:
\[
 A_w=U^{\mathsf T}M_wU,
 \qquad A'_w=U^{\mathsf T}M'_wU.
\]
The lifted-rank margin makes \(S\) invertible, with
\[
 s_{\min}(S)=s_{\min}(V_d)\ge\sigma,
 \qquad \lVert S\rVert\le\lVert V_d\rVert_F=\sqrt n,
 \qquad \operatorname{cond}(S)\le\chi=\frac{\sqrt n}{\sigma}.
\]
Writing
\[
 D_w=\operatorname{diag}\!\left(\lambda_j(u^{\mathsf T}c_j)^{q-1}(w^{\mathsf T}c_j)\right),
\]
the tensor factorization gives \(A_w=SD_wS^{\mathsf T}\). In particular, the cumulant and orientation margins imply
\[
 s_{\min}(A_u)
 \ge s_{\min}(S)^2\min_j|\lambda_j(u^{\mathsf T}c_j)^q|
 \ge\kappa\sigma^{q+2}=\eta,
\]
whereas unit columns and \(|\lambda_j|\le\Lambda\) imply
\[
 \lVert A_w\rVert\le \lVert V_d\rVert^2\Lambda\le n\Lambda.
\]
Since \(\Delta<\eta/2\), the elementary Neumann identity
\[
 A'_u=A_u\{I+A_u^{-1}(A'_u-A_u)\}
\]
shows that \(A'_u\) is invertible and \(\lVert(A'_u)^{-1}\rVert\le2/\eta\). The primed exact factorization is
\[
 A'_u=S'D'_u(S')^{\mathsf T},
 \qquad S'=U^{\mathsf T}V'_d.
\]
Every diagonal entry of \(D'_u\) is nonzero; invertibility of \(A'_u\) therefore forces the square matrix \(S'\) to be invertible.

Define \(G_w=A_wA_u^{-1}\) and \(G'_w=A'_w(A'_u)^{-1}\). The inverse identity and the preceding bounds give
\[
 \begin{aligned}
 \lVert G'_w-G_w\rVert
 &\le \lVert A'_w-A_w\rVert\lVert(A'_u)^{-1}\rVert
   +\lVert A_w\rVert\lVert(A'_u)^{-1}(A_u-A'_u)A_u^{-1}\rVert\\
 &\le\left(\frac2\eta+\frac{2n\Lambda}{\eta^2}\right)\Delta
 =h\Delta.
 \end{aligned}
\]
Exact cancellation of the diagonal factors yields
\[
 G_w=S\operatorname{diag}\!\left(\frac{w^{\mathsf T}c_j}{u^{\mathsf T}c_j}\right)S^{-1},
 \qquad
 G'_w=S'\operatorname{diag}\!\left(\frac{w^{\mathsf T}c'_j}{u^{\mathsf T}c'_j}\right)(S')^{-1}.
\]

We next pair the two spectra without presupposing a label. Let \(\rho_j=v^{\mathsf T}c_j/(u^{\mathsf T}c_j)\), let \(g=\sigma/3\), and let \(\Gamma_j\) be the positively oriented complex circle of radius \(g\) about \(\rho_j\). The gap assumption makes these circles disjoint. For \(z\in\Gamma_j\), diagonalization gives
\[
 \lVert(zI-G_v)^{-1}\rVert\le\frac{\chi}{g}.
\]
For \(G_v(t)=G_v+t(G'_v-G_v)\), \(0\le t\le1\), the condition \(\Delta<\sigma/(6\chi h)\) gives
\[
 \lVert t(G'_v-G_v)(zI-G_v)^{-1}\rVert
 \le \frac{\chi h\Delta}{g}<\frac12.
\]
Thus the Neumann series makes every \(zI-G_v(t)\) invertible and bounds its inverse by \(2\chi/g\). Define entrywise
\[
 P_j(t)=\frac{1}{2\pi\mathrm i}\int_{\Gamma_j}(zI-G_v(t))^{-1}\,dz.
\]
At \(t=0\), direct integration of the displayed diagonalization gives \(P_j(0)=SE_{jj}S^{-1}\), a rank-one projector. The resolvent identity verifies directly that every \(P_j(t)\) is idempotent; it is continuous in \(t\), so its trace, equal to its integer rank, is constantly one. At \(t=1\) the \(n\) disjoint rank-one projectors account for all \(n\) eigenvalues and hence define a permutation pairing of the primed and unprimed components. Relabel the primed components by this permutation and write \(P'_j=P_j(1)\).

The resolvent identity under the same contour bounds yields
\[
 \begin{aligned}
 \lVert P'_j-P_j\rVert
 &\le \frac{1}{2\pi}(2\pi g)
 \frac{\chi}{g}\,h\Delta\,\frac{2\chi}{g}
 =\frac{6\chi^2h}{\sigma}\Delta,\\
 \lVert P_j\rVert&\le\chi,
 \qquad
 \lVert P'_j\rVert\le\lVert P_j\rVert+\lVert P'_j-P_j\rVert<2\chi.
 \end{aligned}
\]
For each coordinate probe, simultaneous diagonalization and cyclicity of trace give
\[
 z_{ij}:=\operatorname{tr}(G_{e_i}P_j)=\frac{c_{ij}}{u^{\mathsf T}c_j},
 \qquad
 z'_{ij}:=\operatorname{tr}(G'_{e_i}P'_j)=\frac{c'_{ij}}{u^{\mathsf T}c'_j}.
\]
Since \(|\operatorname{tr}K|\le n\lVert K\rVert\) and \(\lVert G_{e_i}\rVert\le n\Lambda/\eta\),
\[
 \begin{aligned}
 |z'_{ij}-z_{ij}|
 &\le n\lVert G'_{e_i}-G_{e_i}\rVert\lVert P'_j\rVert
 +n\lVert G_{e_i}\rVert\lVert P'_j-P_j\rVert\\
 &\le nh\left(2\chi+\frac{6n\Lambda\chi^2}{\eta\sigma}\right)\Delta
 =L_z\Delta.
 \end{aligned}
\]
The orientation and unit-normalization conditions give
\[
 \lVert z_j\rVert_2=(u^{\mathsf T}c_j)^{-1}\ge1,
 \qquad
 \lVert z'_j\rVert_2=(u^{\mathsf T}c'_j)^{-1}\ge1,
\]
and \(c_j=z_j/\lVert z_j\rVert_2\), with the same formula for \(c'_j\). For nonzero vectors of norm at least one, adding and subtracting the common denominator shows
\[
 \left\lVert\frac{z'}{\lVert z'\rVert_2}-\frac{z}{\lVert z\rVert_2}\right\rVert_2
 \le2\lVert z'-z\rVert_2.
\]
Hence each paired column obeys \(\lVert c'_j-c_j\rVert_2\le2\sqrt p L_z\Delta\), and summing squared column bounds gives
\[
 \lVert C'_{\pi}-C\rVert_F
 \le2\sqrt{np}L_z\Delta=L_C\Delta.
\]
The projector-trace formulas are exactly the declared map \(\operatorname{OICAInv}\); applying them with each tensor's own range basis changes only the diagonalizing coordinates and returns the same normalized directions. Thus that map recovers the directions attaining the bound.

semantic_closure.statement: Under the population assumptions, \(J_x(C)\ne\varnothing\) and the sharp equilibrium-effect set over the entire source-minimal fixed-law fiber is \[\{\theta_{y\leftarrow x}(\mathcal M):\mathcal M\in\mathfrak F_x(C,\varepsilon)\}=\mathcal R_{xy}(C)=\{C_{yj}/C_{xj}:C_{xj}\ne0,\ \operatorname{rank}(C_{-x,-j})=p-1\}.\] All values and one exact witness per value are certifiable in \(O(n^4)\) arithmetic operations.
semantic_closure.justification: The theorem replaces a large cyclic graph equivalence class by an exact finite, query-specific effect frontier with constructive sharpness.
semantic_closure.gap: DaiAlbrechtSpirtesZhang2026 characterizes graph-indexed distribution families, and TramontanoDrtonEtesami2026 gives partial coefficient criteria for known mixed graphs; neither identifies the image of every completion of one numerical overcomplete-ICA law.
semantic_closure.consumer: For the fourteen-stock Hong Kong example of DaiAlbrechtSpirtesZhang2026, it compresses \(19{,}008\) compatible graphs into the exact source-ratio answers for any selected ordered stock pair.
semantic_closure.proof_tex:
The source assumptions ensure that the supplied representation and every monomially rescaled disturbance system remain within the stated source-minimal non-Gaussian fixed-law setting; the algebraic sharpness argument itself uses the full-row-rank and solvability conditions explicitly.

First, \(J_x(C)\) is nonempty. Extend \(C\) to \(T_0\) and write \(W_0=T_0^{-1}\), as in the witness construction. The \((x,x)\) entry of \(T_0W_0=I_n\) is
\[
 1=\sum_{j=1}^n C_{xj}(W_0)_{jx}. \tag{10}
\]
Thus some \(j\) satisfies \(C_{xj}(W_0)_{jx}\ne0\). The inverse-cofactor formula then implies \(\det((T_0)_{-x,-j})\ne0\). The observed rows other than \(x\), restricted away from column \(j\), are a subset of the rows of this nonsingular minor, so \(\operatorname{rank}(C_{-x,-j})=p-1\). Together with \(C_{xj}\ne0\), this proves \(j\in J_x(C)\).

For the first set inclusion, take any \(\mathcal M\in\mathfrak F_x(C,\varepsilon)\). The necessary-deletion-rank lemma gives \(s_{\mathcal M}(x)\in J_x(C)\), and the intervention-ratio lemma gives
\[
 \theta_{y\leftarrow x}(\mathcal M)
 =\frac{C_{y,s_{\mathcal M}(x)}}{C_{x,s_{\mathcal M}(x)}}
 \in\mathcal R_{xy}(C). \tag{11}
\]
Conversely, if \(r_0\in\mathcal R_{xy}(C)\), then by definition \(r_0=C_{yj}/C_{xj}\) for some \(j\in J_x(C)\). The shear-and-matching sufficiency lemma returns \(\mathcal M_j\in\mathfrak F_x(C,\varepsilon)\) with assigned source \(j\), and the intervention-ratio lemma yields \(\theta_{y\leftarrow x}(\mathcal M_j)=r_0\). This proves the reverse inclusion and constructive sharpness.

For the arithmetic bound, one Gaussian elimination extends the \(p\) rows of \(C\) and inverts \(T_0\) in \(O(n^3)\) operations. Criterion (5) in the sufficiency proof classifies all \(j\) by scanning row \(j\) of \(W_0\), so all deletion decisions cost \(O(n^2)\) after the inverse. For each of at most \(n\) admissible indices, the shear costs \(O(n^2)\), a perfect matching in the \((n-1)\)-by-\((n-1)\) nonzero pattern can be found by an augmenting-path algorithm in \(O(n^3)\), and row normalization costs \(O(n^2)\). Hence all witnesses cost \(O(n^4)\) arithmetic operations. Exact zero tests are part of the real-arithmetic model; this is not a floating-point or bit-complexity claim. Selecting one representative \(j\) for each distinct ratio returns one exact witness per distinct value.

semantic_closure.statement: For every \(N\) and every nonempty class \(\mathfrak P_{p,n,r}(a,\delta,\sigma,\kappa,\Lambda,M)\) with \(d\ge1\), \(q\ge1\), and \(n\le\binom{p+d-1}{d}\), the iid confidence unions satisfy \[\inf_{\zeta=(P_X,C,\varepsilon,\lambda)\in\mathfrak P_{p,n,r}}P_X^{\otimes N}\!\left\{\begin{array}{l}\mathcal R_{xy}(C)\subseteq\mathcal U_{xy}\text{ for every }x\ne y\in\mathsf O,\\ \text{and, if }2\tau_N<\epsilon_0\text{ and }b_N<\min\{a,\delta\}/2,\text{ then after one common permutation}\\ \widehat J_x=J_x(C)\text{ and }d_H(\mathcal U_{xy},\mathcal R_{xy}(C))\le2w_N\text{ for every }x\ne y\in\mathsf O\end{array}\right\}\ge1-\alpha.\] Uniformly over the same representation-indexed tuples in the informative regime, \(2w_N=O(N^{-1/2})\).
semantic_closure.justification: The theorem makes the finite causal frontier inferentially usable and measures uncertainty by Hausdorff error rather than by the nonshrinking diameter of a genuinely multivalued set.
semantic_closure.gap: Existing OICA papers recover directions or bound component error, but no located paper gives simultaneous uniform coverage and root-\(N\) Hausdorff uncertainty for a rank-selected finite causal frontier.
semantic_closure.consumer: It supports honest iid uncertainty reports for laboratory or cross-sectional latent systems whose source directions satisfy an empirical separation certificate.
semantic_closure.proof_tex:
Fix a tuple \(\zeta\in\mathfrak P_{p,n,r}(a,\delta,\sigma,\kappa,\Lambda,M)\). Unit normalization gives
\[
 \lVert X\rVert_2\le\sum_{j=1}^n|\varepsilon_j|.
\]
The convexity inequality \((\sum_j t_j)^{2r}\le n^{2r-1}\sum_jt_j^{2r}\), followed by the source-moment envelope, yields
\[
 \mathbb E\lVert X\rVert_2^{2r}
 \le n^{2r-1}\sum_{j=1}^n\mathbb E|\varepsilon_j|^{2r}
 \le n^{2r}M\le H. \tag{13}
\]
Let \(\mu\in\mathbb R^m\) collect the nonconstant raw moments through total degree \(r\), and let \(\widetilde\mu\) be their untrimmed empirical averages. If a coordinate has degree \(k\le r\), its squared monomial is bounded by \(1+\lVert X\rVert_2^{2r}\). Thus (13) gives variance at most \(1+H\) for every coordinate and
\[
 \mathbb E\lVert\widetilde\mu-\mu\rVert_2^2
 \le\frac{m(1+H)}{N}. \tag{14}
\]
Moreover every true coordinate has absolute value at most \((1+H)^{1/2}\le B_m\). Coordinatewise clipping to \([-B_m,B_m]\) is projection onto an interval containing the true coordinate, so it cannot increase the Euclidean error. Markov's inequality applied to (14) therefore proves, for
\[
 E_N=\{\lVert\widehat\mu-\mu\rVert_2\le e_N\},
\qquad
 \inf_{\zeta\in\mathfrak P_{p,n,r}}P_X^{\otimes N}(E_N)\ge1-\alpha. \tag{15}
\]

For an ordered tensor coordinate, the moment--cumulant formula is
\[
 \operatorname{cum}(X_{i_1},\ldots,X_{i_r})
 =\sum_{\pi\in\mathfrak P_r}(-1)^{|\pi|-1}(|\pi|-1)!
   \prod_{A\in\pi}\mathbb E\!\left[\prod_{k\in A}X_{i_k}\right]. \tag{16}
\]
On the moment box \([-B_m,B_m]^m\), telescoping a product with \(|\pi|\) factors bounds its change by \(|\pi|B_m^{|\pi|-1}\lVert\widehat\mu-\mu\rVert_2\). There are \(p^r\) ordered tensor coordinates, so (16) and the Frobenius norm give, on \(E_N\),
\[
 \lVert\widehat{\mathcal T}_r-\mathcal T_r\rVert_F
 \le p^{r/2}\sum_{\pi\in\mathfrak P_r}(|\pi|-1)!|\pi|B_m^{|\pi|-1}e_N
 =\tau_N. \tag{17}
\]

The true normalized factor pair is feasible for the minimum-distance problem. The feasible numerical restrictions are closed and bounded: the columns lie on unit spheres, the cumulants lie in the compact set \(\{t:\kappa\le|t|\le\Lambda\}\), and all singular-value, loading, and pencil-gap restrictions are closed. Nonemptiness is assumed. Hence a minimizer exists, and the fixed lexicographic selection makes \((\widehat C,\widehat\lambda)\) a statistic. Its optimality and (17) imply
\[
 \left\lVert\sum_j\widehat\lambda_j\widehat c_j^{\otimes r}
       -\mathcal T_r\right\rVert_F
 \le 2\tau_N. \tag{18}
\]
The deterministic tensor-pencil argument in the common-order local-inverse lemma uses only the numerical restrictions imposed on these two factor pairs. Therefore, if \(2\tau_N<\epsilon_0\), (18) supplies one common permutation under which
\[
 \lVert\widehat C-C\rVert_F\le 2L_C\tau_N=b_N. \tag{19}
\]

Suppose also \(b_N<\min\{a,\delta\}/2\). Both \(C\) and the feasible fit obey the alternative that each loading is zero or has magnitude at least \(a\). Hence (19) prevents a zero loading in either matrix from being paired with a nonzero loading in the other. The zero patterns agree. For every deletion matrix, Weyl's singular-value inequality and (19) give
\[
 \left|s_{\min}(\widehat C_{-i,-j})-s_{\min}(C_{-i,-j})\right|
 \le\lVert\widehat C-C\rVert_F<\delta/2.
\]
Because each of the two feasible singular values is either zero or at least \(\delta\), their zero status agrees. Consequently \(\widehat J_x=J_x(C)\) simultaneously for every observed \(x\).

For \(j\in J_x(C)=\widehat J_x\), both denominators have magnitude at least \(a\), while unit normalization bounds \(|C_{yj}|\le1\). Using (19) coordinatewise gives
\[
 \left|\frac{\widehat C_{yj}}{\widehat C_{xj}}-\frac{C_{yj}}{C_{xj}}\right|
 \le \frac{|\widehat C_{yj}-C_{yj}|}{|\widehat C_{xj}|}
 +\frac{|C_{yj}|\,|\widehat C_{xj}-C_{xj}|}{|\widehat C_{xj}|\,|C_{xj}|}
 \le(a^{-1}+a^{-2})b_N=w_N. \tag{20}
\]
Thus every true ratio belongs to its interval in \(\mathcal U_{xy}\). Conversely, every point of that interval is within \(w_N\) of its estimated center and, by (20), within another \(w_N\) of the corresponding true ratio. Hence
\[
 \mathcal R_{xy}(C)\subseteq\mathcal U_{xy},
 \qquad
 d_H(\mathcal U_{xy},\mathcal R_{xy}(C))\le2w_N \tag{21}
\]
simultaneously for all \(x\ne y\). If either deterministic informative-regime inequality fails, the definition gives \(\mathcal U_{xy}=[-a^{-1},a^{-1}]\); every admissible ratio lies in this interval because its numerator is at most one and its denominator is at least \(a\). Coverage therefore holds in both regimes on the single event \(E_N\), and (15) proves the displayed uniform probability bound. Finally, with dimensions, margins, \(M\), and \(\alpha\) fixed, \(L_m\), \(L_C\), and \(H\) are constants, so \(\tau_N=O(N^{-1/2})\) and \(2w_N=O(N^{-1/2})\).

semantic_closure.construction: \(\mathfrak P_{p,n,r}(a,\delta,\sigma,\kappa,\Lambda,M)=\{\zeta=(P_X,C,\varepsilon,\lambda):X=C\varepsilon\in\mathbb R^p,\ C\in\mathbb R^{p\times n},\lambda_j=\operatorname{cum}_r(\varepsilon_j),\ d\ge1,\ q\ge1,\ r=2d+q,\ n\le\binom{p+d-1}{d},\text{ and the listed source, normalization, cumulant, tensor, moment, loading, and deletion-margin properties hold for the indices }p,n,r,d,q\}\)

semantic_closure.statement: For every \(\mathcal M\in\mathfrak F_x(C,\varepsilon)\), its assigned source satisfies \(s_{\mathcal M}(x)\in J_x(C)\)
semantic_closure.justification: Deletion rank is the observable obstruction that rules out source assignments incompatible with a legal intervention.
semantic_closure.gap: DaiAlbrechtSpirtesZhang2026 uses graph-level edge ranks and children bases, not numerical row-and-column deletion ranks for a fixed law.
semantic_closure.consumer: It provides a falsifiable certificate that removes impossible effect values before any completion is constructed.
semantic_closure.proof_tex:
Fix \(\mathcal M=(Q,H)\in\mathfrak F_x(C,\varepsilon)\), set \(j=s_{\mathcal M}(x)\), and let \(h=H_{xj}\ne0\). Define
\[
 T=Q^{-1}H,\qquad W=T^{-1}=H^{-1}Q.
\]
By the fixed-law condition, \(T_{\mathsf O,:}=C\). Since \(H\) is monomial and its entry in row \(x\), column \(j\) is \(h\), row \(j\) of \(H^{-1}\) has its unique nonzero entry \(h^{-1}\) in column \(x\). The unit structural diagonal consequently implies
\[
 W_{jx}=(H^{-1}Q)_{jx}=h^{-1}Q_{xx}=h^{-1}\ne0. \tag{3}
\]
The inverse-cofactor formula for \(W=T^{-1}\) now gives
\[
 W_{jx}=\frac{(-1)^{j+x}\det(T_{-x,-j})}{\det(T)}.
\]
Because both \(W_{jx}\) and \(\det(T)\) are nonzero, \(T_{-x,-j}\) is nonsingular. Its rows indexed by \(\mathsf O\setminus\{x\}\) are precisely the \(p-1\) rows of \(C_{-x,-j}\); a subset of the rows of a nonsingular matrix is linearly independent. Hence
\[
 \operatorname{rank}(C_{-x,-j})=p-1. \tag{4}
\]
Finally, as in the adjugate calculation for the intervention ratio,
\[
 C_{xj}=(Q^{-1})_{xx}h
 =\frac{\det(Q_{-x,-x})}{\det(Q)}h\ne0,
\]
using observational and postintervention solvability. Equations (4) and the last display are exactly the two membership conditions for \(j\in J_x(C)\).

semantic_closure.statement: For every \(j\in J_x(C)\), \(\operatorname{Cert}(C,x)\) returns a completion \(\mathcal M_j\in\mathfrak F_x(C,\varepsilon)\) with \(s_{\mathcal M_j}(x)=j\). If \(C\) is rational, the returned \(Q_j\) and \(H_j\) are rational.
semantic_closure.justification: This is the nontrivial converse: one latent-row shear and one perfect matching realize every admissible ratio without changing the observed law.
semantic_closure.gap: The matching construction of DaiAlbrechtSpirtesZhang2026 concerns compatible graph families; LacerdaSpirtesRamseyHoyer2008 has square row permutations and no latent-row shear.
semantic_closure.consumer: It yields exact audit models demonstrating that an apparent effect ambiguity is structural rather than numerical.
semantic_closure.proof_tex:
Because \(C\) has row rank \(p\), its rows extend to a basis of \(\mathbb R^n\); choose such an extension \(T_0\in\operatorname{GL}_n(\mathbb R)\) with \((T_0)_{\mathsf O,:}=C\), and put \(W_0=T_0^{-1}\). We first record the elementary deletion criterion
\[
 \operatorname{rank}(C_{-x,-j})<p-1
 \quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad
 e_j^{\top}\in\operatorname{rowspan}(C_{-x,:})
 \quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad
 (W_0)_{jx}=0\ \text{ and }\ (W_0)_{j\ell}=0\ \text{ for every }\ell\in\mathsf L. \tag{5}
\]
For the first equivalence, the \(p-1\) rows of \(C_{-x,:}\) are independent because they are a subset of the independent rows of \(C\). Their restrictions to the coordinates other than \(j\) are dependent exactly when a nonzero linear combination is supported only at coordinate \(j\); independence before restriction makes that combination a nonzero multiple of \(e_j^{\top}\). For the second equivalence, the identity \(W_0T_0=I_n\) gives the unique expansion
\[
 e_j^{\top}=\sum_{i=1}^n (W_0)_{ji}(T_0)_{i,:}.
\]
It belongs to the span of the observed rows other than \(x\) exactly when its coefficients on row \(x\) and on all latent rows vanish. This proves (5).

Now fix \(j\in J_x(C)\). If \((W_0)_{jx}\ne0\), set \(T=T_0\) and \(W=W_0\). If \((W_0)_{jx}=0\), the full deletion rank in the definition of \(J_x(C)\), together with (5), supplies \(\ell\in\mathsf L\) with \((W_0)_{j\ell}\ne0\). Define
\[
 T=(I_n+e_\ell e_x^{\top})T_0,
 \qquad
 W=W_0(I_n-e_\ell e_x^{\top}). \tag{6}
\]
Since \(x\ne\ell\), \((e_\ell e_x^{\top})^2=0\), so the two shear matrices in (6) are inverse and \(W=T^{-1}\). The shear changes only latent row \(\ell\), hence \(T_{\mathsf O,:}=C\), and
\[
 W_{jx}=(W_0)_{jx}-(W_0)_{j\ell}=-(W_0)_{j\ell}\ne0. \tag{7}
\]
When \(n=p\), the set \(\mathsf L\) is empty and (5) shows directly that the second case cannot occur.

Since \(W^{-1}=T\) and \(T_{xj}=C_{xj}\ne0\), the cofactor identity gives
\[
 (-1)^{j+x}\det(W_{-j,-x})
 =\operatorname{cof}(W)_{jx}
 =\det(W)(W^{-1})_{xj}
 =\det(W)C_{xj}\ne0. \tag{8}
\]
Thus \(W_{-j,-x}\) is nonsingular. In the determinant expansion of this matrix, at least one permutation term is nonzero. Its nonzero entries give a perfect matching between the rows other than \(j\) and the columns other than \(x\). Augment that matching by assigning row \(j\) to column \(x\), and let \(\Pi\) be the row-permutation matrix placing every matched row in its matched column. All diagonal entries of \(\Pi W\) are nonzero. Therefore
\[
 D=\operatorname{diag}(\Pi W),\qquad
 Q=D^{-1}\Pi W,\qquad
 H=D^{-1}\Pi \tag{9}
\]
are well defined. The matrix \(H\) is monomial, \(Q\) is invertible, and (9) gives \(Q_{ii}=1\) for all \(i\). Moreover,
\[
 Q^{-1}H
 =W^{-1}\Pi^{-1}D D^{-1}\Pi
 =T,
\]
so \([Q^{-1}H]_{\mathsf O,:}=T_{\mathsf O,:}=C\). Row \(x\) of \(H\) has its unique nonzero entry in column \(j\), whence \(s_{\mathcal M_j}(x)=j\). Finally, deleting row and column \(x\) in (9) gives, up to the complementary row permutation,
\[
 Q_{-x,-x}=D_{-x,-x}^{-1}(\Pi W)_{-x,-x},
\]
and \((\Pi W)_{-x,-x}\) is a row permutation of the nonsingular matrix \(W_{-j,-x}\) from (8). Hence \(\det(Q_{-x,-x})\ne0\). All defining conditions of \(\mathfrak F_x(C,\varepsilon)\) have now been verified.

If \(C\) is rational, Gaussian elimination can extend its rows using rational coordinate rows, so \(T_0\), \(W_0\), and the shear in (6) are rational. The permutation is integral, every entry of \(D\) is a nonzero rational number, and (9) uses only rational arithmetic and division by those entries. Thus the returned \(Q_j\) and \(H_j\) are rational.

payload.statement: Suppose that \((n,C,\varepsilon)\) is an irreducible ICA representation of \(P_X\), every coordinate of \(\varepsilon\) is non-Gaussian, and \((m_{\mathcal M},A^{\mathcal M},\xi^{\mathcal M})\in\mathfrak I(P_X)\) is any other irreducible ICA representation. payload.statement: Let \((C,\lambda)\) and \((C',\lambda')\) be two normalized numerical factor pairs satisfying all cumulant-magnitude, probe-orientation, lifted-rank, pencil-gap, and dimensional restrictions in the definition of \(\mathfrak P_{p,n,r}(a,\delta,\sigma,\kappa,\Lambda,M)\), and let \(\mathcal T_r=\sum_j\lambda_jc_j^{\otimes r}\) and \(\mathcal T'_r=\sum_j\lambda'_j(c'_j)^{\otimes r}\). If \(\lVert\mathcal T'_r-\mathcal T_r\rVert_F<\epsilon_0\), then a permutation \(\pi\) exists such that \(\lVert C'_{\pi}-C\rVert_F\le L_C\lVert\mathcal T'_r-\mathcal T_r\rVert_F\). Thus the local inverse bound applies to the numerical feasible set of the minimum-distance fit, without requiring the fitted factors to be accompanied by a source law.
payload.proof_tex:
Put \(e=\lVert\mathcal T'_r-\mathcal T_r\rVert_F\). Contract the last \(q\) modes against \(u^{\otimes(q-1)}\otimes w\), matricize the remaining modes in two blocks of degree \(d\), and denote the resulting matrices by \(M_w,M'_w\). Contraction by unit vectors, matricization, and orthogonal compression do not increase Frobenius norm, so every compressed difference below has operator norm at most \(e\).

Let \(U\) be an orthonormal basis for \(\operatorname{range}(V_d)\), and set
\[
 S=U^\top V_d,
 \qquad A_w=U^\top M_wU
 =S\operatorname{diag}\!\left(\lambda_j(u^\top c_j)^{q-1}(w^\top c_j)\right)S^\top. \tag{23}
\]
The lifted-rank margin gives \(s_{\min}(S)=s_{\min}(V_d)\ge\sigma\), while \(\lVert S\rVert\le\lVert V_d\rVert_F=\sqrt n\). For \(w=u\), every diagonal magnitude in (23) is at least \(\kappa\sigma^q\). Hence
\[
 s_{\min}(A_u)\ge\kappa\sigma^q s_{\min}(S)^2
 \ge\kappa\sigma^{q+2}=\eta,
 \qquad \lVert A_u^{-1}\rVert\le\eta^{-1}. \tag{24}
\]
The same factorization also gives \(\lVert A_w\rVert\le n\Lambda\) for every unit \(w\).

Compress the primed contractions using this same \(U\), so \(A'_w=U^\top M'_wU\) and \(\lVert A'_w-A_w\rVert\le e\). Since \(e<\eta/2\), (24) and the Neumann series imply
\[
 \lVert(A'_u)^{-1}\rVert\le2\eta^{-1}. \tag{25}
\]
Writing \(S'=U^\top V'_d\), the factorization \(A'_u=S'D'_u(S')^\top\), with nonsingular diagonal \(D'_u\), and invertibility of \(A'_u\) show that \(S'\) is invertible. Therefore, for \(G_w=A_wA_u^{-1}\) and \(G'_w=A'_w(A'_u)^{-1}\),
\[
 G_w=S\operatorname{diag}\!\left(\frac{w^\top c_j}{u^\top c_j}\right)S^{-1},
 \quad
 G'_w=S'\operatorname{diag}\!\left(\frac{w^\top c'_j}{u^\top c'_j}\right)(S')^{-1}. \tag{26}
\]
The inverse identity and (24)--(25) give
\[
 \lVert G'_w-G_w\rVert
 \le\left(\frac{2}{\eta}+\frac{2n\Lambda}{\eta^2}\right)e
 =he. \tag{27}
\]

For \(w=v\), the eigenvalues of \(G_v\) are real and pairwise separated by at least \(\sigma\). Around each eigenvalue draw a complex circle of radius \(g=\sigma/3\). From (26), the resolvent on a circle is bounded by \(\chi/g\), where \(\chi=\lVert S\rVert\lVert S^{-1}\rVert\le\sqrt n/\sigma\). The condition \(e<\sigma/(6\chi h)\) makes \((\chi/g)he<1/2\). The resolvent identity and Neumann series therefore show that every circle contains exactly one eigenvalue of \(G'_v\), counted algebraically, and that the corresponding rank-one spectral projectors satisfy
\[
 \lVert P'_j-P_j\rVert
 \le \frac{2\chi^2he}{g}
 =\frac{6\chi^2he}{\sigma},
 \qquad
 \lVert P_j\rVert\le\chi,
 \qquad
 \lVert P'_j\rVert\le2\chi. \tag{28}
\]
Indeed, integrate \((zI-G'_v)^{-1}(G'_v-G_v)(zI-G_v)^{-1}\) around the circle; its length divided by \(2\pi\) is \(g\), which gives (28). Continuity along \(G_v+t(G'_v-G_v)\) and the integer-valued rank of a projector justify the one-eigenvalue pairing. This supplies one common permutation \(\pi\).

For each coordinate vector \(e_i\), define \(z_{ij}=\operatorname{tr}(G_{e_i}P_j)\) and define \(z'_{i,\pi(j)}\) analogously. Simultaneous diagonalization in (26) gives
\[
 z_j=\frac{c_j}{u^\top c_j},
 \qquad
 z'_{\pi(j)}=\frac{c'_{\pi(j)}}{u^\top c'_{\pi(j)}}. \tag{29}
\]
Using \(|\operatorname{tr}(R)|\le n\lVert R\rVert\), \(\lVert G_{e_i}\rVert\le n\Lambda/\eta\), and (27)--(28), we obtain coordinatewise
\[
 |z'_{i,\pi(j)}-z_{ij}|
 \le nh\left(2\chi+\frac{6n\Lambda\chi^2}{\eta\sigma}\right)e
 =L_ze. \tag{30}
\]
The probe orientation fixes the sign in (29), and unit normalization gives \(\lVert z_j\rVert=1/(u^\top c_j)\ge1\), with the same statement for \(z'_{\pi(j)}\). Normalization on vectors of norm at least one is two-Lipschitz, so (30) yields
\[
 \lVert c'_{\pi(j)}-c_j\rVert_2
 \le2\sqrt p\,L_ze. \tag{31}
\]
Squaring (31), summing over \(j\), and taking square roots proves
\[
 \lVert C'_{\pi}-C\rVert_F
 \le2\sqrt{np}\,L_ze=L_Ce.
\]
Only the displayed numerical restrictions were used, which proves the extension to the estimator's feasible factor set.

payload.reason: The monomial disturbance map is the published one-shock-per-equation LiNG class, not a novel convention; the new object is the law-conditioned query projection.

novel.justification: This is the law-conditioned query convention: structural uncertainty ranges over every irreducible one-shock-per-equation completion entailing the same observed law, while ICA uniqueness proves rather than assumes agreement of source directions.

payload.reason: The old condition fixed one mixing representation; the directive requires equality only of the induced observed law.

proposed.comparator_claim: Section 4 constructs square candidates by admissible row permutation and row normalization, while Theorem 1 states distribution-entailment equivalence of the LiNG-D output; it does not assert solvability after a specified intervention.

Appendix B.1, Lemma 11 restates the all-non-Gaussian irreducible-ICA result that equal observed laws have equal source counts and the same mixing directions up to scaling and permutation; the main results characterize graph-indexed distributional equivalence.
The total-effect theorem gives a complete graphical criterion for generic effect identification in acyclic latent-variable LiNGAM, not a cyclic numerical law-fiber response set.
The cyclic section gives a necessary coefficient-identification condition in general and a complete result for restricted cycle structures, conditional on a known mixed graph.

The introduction records Eriksson--Koivunen Theorem 3: with no Gaussian source, absence of collinear mixing columns is exactly the population identifiability condition up to column scaling and permutation; Wang--Seigal's main theorem treats the remaining overcomplete case with one Gaussian source.
Theorem 4a gives essential uniqueness of a three-factor tensor decomposition under the Kruskal-rank inequality.
The paper develops robust tensor-decomposition methods under quantitative nondegeneracy conditions.
The finite-cumulant-sequence theorem implies that a nondegenerate non-Gaussian law with all moments has infinitely many nonzero higher cumulants.

payload.reason: The table now matches the published Wang--Seigal/Eriksson--Koivunen full-law uniqueness input and distinguishes it from the new causal response projection.

payload.tldr: For an irreducible all-non-Gaussian observed law, every source-minimal cyclic one-shock-per-equation completion has the same source directions up to permutation and scaling. Its sharp response to one hard intervention is therefore the finite vector set \(\mathcal R_x^{\mathrm{vec}}(C)=\{C_{-x,j}/C_{xj}:j\in J_x(C)\}\); scalar effects are coordinate projections of these same vectors. One latent-row shear and one perfect matching construct every same-law witness in \(O(n^4)\) total arithmetic operations. A separated common-order iid class admits simultaneous scalar intervals and source-indexed Euclidean response balls with uniform coverage and root-\(N\) Hausdorff uncertainty. Without a common active cumulant order, exact population recovery starts at order \(2n-1\), obeys the adaptive elbow \(2R_\nu-1\), and stops at a finite model-specific order, but no uniform finite order or uniform inference rate exists under qualitative moment determinacy alone.

project_justification.gap: Published all-non-Gaussian ICA theory identifies the source count and directions from the full observed law, and published latent cyclic LiNG work characterizes graph-level distributional equivalence. Neither computes the exact hard-intervention response-vector image of every irreducible, source-minimal, postintervention-solvable completion entailing one observed law.
project_justification.niche: Law-level ICA uniqueness reduces every alternative completion to a permutation and scaling of one recovered direction matrix. The deletion-rank map is invariant under those indeterminacies and preserves all outcomes attached to the same source, so the causal query can be solved without graph enumeration or dynamical stability.
project_justification.fill: The note proves the sharp response-vector and scalar frontiers over the full irreducible observational-law fiber, constructs all witnesses and exact countermodels, characterizes vector and coordinatewise point identification, gives an \(O(n^4)\) certificate, establishes simultaneous scalar/vector iid confidence unions, and derives the adaptive heterogeneous-order population inverse and its uniform-impossibility boundary.

sampling_model.design: Observational iid sampling under \(P_X^{\otimes N}\) for each separated representation-indexed tuple \(\zeta=(P_X,C,\varepsilon,\lambda)\). The causal estimand ranges over the full irreducible observational-law fiber; published ICA uniqueness proves that its deletion-rank frontier is invariant to the chosen normalized representation.
sampling_model.units: \(N\) independent copies of \(X=C\varepsilon\) under \(P_X^{\otimes N}\), indexed by one tuple \(\zeta\in\mathfrak P_{p,n,r}(a,\delta,\sigma,\kappa,\Lambda,M)\).
sampling_model.treatment: A single hard intervention replaces the structural equation for observed coordinate \(x\) by \(V_x=t\); the target is the joint equilibrium response of all other observed coordinates. This is not a claim about simultaneous interventions on several treatment coordinates.
sampling_model.overlap: Not applicable; the relevant regularity conditions are the treatment-loading, deletion-singular-value, lifted-rank, cumulant, and pencil-separation margins.
sampling_model.nuisance_estimation: Normalized mixing directions are recovered by the common-order cumulant tensor pencil and a separated minimum-distance fit. One common source permutation aligns the whole response vector; no outcome-wise relabeling is permitted.

payload.interpretation: A point of \(\mathcal R_x^{\mathrm{vec}}(C)\) is one jointly attainable equilibrium response vector from a single structural completion. Its coordinates may be reported as scalar frontiers, but values from different source indices cannot be combined into a fictitious cross-outcome vector. Pairwise nonproportional directions imply that the whole response vector is point identified exactly when one source passes the deletion-rank test; an individual outcome may still be point identified when several admissible sources share that one slope. For the fourteen-stock HSI example, the method would attach at most one vector per recovered source direction to a chosen stock intervention and can return two exact models when those vectors differ. No numerical HSI effect or confidence ball is asserted here.
payload.technical_internal_limitation: The observational-law enlargement is limited to irreducible ICA representations and source-minimal LiNG completions with one independent shock per equation. Reducible representations, zero or duplicated/proportional directions, shock splitting or merging, and merely graphical irreducibility without this source-minimal representation condition are excluded because the published ICA uniqueness theorem does not identify those fibers and the frontier can change. The \(O(n^4)\) certificate uses exact real arithmetic after \(C\) is available and is not a bit-complexity or floating-point guarantee. Common-order inference assumes fixed moment, tensor-rank, pencil-gap, deletion-rank, and denominator margins; the constrained fit is specified statistically but no polynomial-time global optimizer is claimed. The HSI daily series is dependent and may exhibit mechanism changes, so it supports only a population illustration unless a time-series concentration theorem and an informative empirical separation certificate are supplied.
payload.honest_scope: The population theorem covers the full observational-law fiber of irreducible, source-minimal, one-shock-per-equation cyclic LiNG completions satisfying observational and specified-treatment postintervention solvability, with no stability restriction. It returns the full response to one intervention and all scalar coordinate projections, not a Cartesian product and not a joint multiple-intervention effect. Published all-non-Gaussian ICA uniqueness is an input, not a contribution. The new population inverse for heterogeneous source-specific cumulant orders is exact and stops after a finite model-specific order, beginning universally at \(2n-1\) and at the adaptive elbow \(2R_\nu-1\) for an active rank \(R_\nu\); only a uniform stopping order and uniform inference over the qualitative class are impossible. Uniform root-\(N\) confidence claims are restricted to the declared common-order separated iid class. Stability-refined fibers, reducible or split-source completions, unknown source count, data-selected probes without a new uniform argument, dependent-time-series HSI inference, and favorable empirical constants remain outside scope.
