added_lemmas.statement:
Let \(\widetilde C=C\Pi D\), where \(\Pi e_k=e_{\pi(k)}\) for a permutation \(\pi\) of \(\mathsf S\) and \(D=\operatorname{diag}(d_1,\ldots,d_n)\) with every \(d_k\ne0\). Then \(k\in J_x(\widetilde C)\) if and only if \(\pi(k)\in J_x(C)\), and for every such \(k\),
\[
 \frac{\widetilde C_{-x,k}}{\widetilde C_{xk}}
 =\frac{C_{-x,\pi(k)}}{C_{x,\pi(k)}}.
\]
Consequently \(\mathcal R_x^{\mathrm{vec}}(\widetilde C)=\mathcal R_x^{\mathrm{vec}}(C)\) and \(\mathcal R_{xy}(\widetilde C)=\mathcal R_{xy}(C)\) for every \(y\in\mathsf O\setminus\{x\}\).
added_lemmas.proof_tex:
By the convention \(\Pi e_k=e_{\pi(k)}\), the \(k\)-th column of \(\widetilde C\) is
\[
 \widetilde C_{:,k}=d_k C_{:,\pi(k)}. \tag{1}
\]
Since \(d_k\ne0\), equation (1) gives
\[
 \widetilde C_{xk}\ne0
 \quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad
 C_{x,\pi(k)}\ne0. \tag{2}
\]
After deleting column \(k\), the remaining columns of \(\widetilde C_{-x,-k}\) are obtained from those of \(C_{-x,-\pi(k)}\) by a column permutation and multiplication by a nonsingular diagonal matrix. Both operations preserve row rank, and hence
\[
 \operatorname{rank}(\widetilde C_{-x,-k})
 =\operatorname{rank}(C_{-x,-\pi(k)}). \tag{3}
\]
Equations (2)--(3) and the definition of \(J_x\) prove the membership equivalence. Dividing the \((-x)\)-coordinates of (1) by its \(x\)-coordinate cancels \(d_k\) and proves the displayed response-ratio identity. Because \(\pi\) is bijective, taking the images of the two admissible-index sets gives equality of the vector frontiers. Taking coordinate \(y\) gives equality of the scalar frontiers by their definitions.

added_lemmas.statement:
For every \(\mathcal M=(m_{\mathcal M},Q,H,\xi^{\mathcal M})\in\mathfrak F_x(P_X)\), put \(A=A^{\mathcal M}\) and \(k=s_{\mathcal M}(x)\). Then
\[
 A_{xk}\ne0,
 \qquad \operatorname{rank}(A_{-x,-k})=p-1,
 \qquad \boldsymbol\theta_{\leftarrow x}(\mathcal M)=\frac{A_{-x,k}}{A_{xk}},
 \qquad \theta_{y\leftarrow x}(\mathcal M)=\frac{A_{yk}}{A_{xk}}.
\]
added_lemmas.proof_tex:
Fix \(\mathcal M\) in the stated fiber and abbreviate \(m=m_{\mathcal M}\). Membership in \(\mathfrak F_x(P_X)\) gives \(Q_{ii}=1\), monomial \(H\), \(\det(Q)\ne0\), and \(\det(Q_{-x,-x})\ne0\). Let \(k=s_{\mathcal M}(x)\) and \(h=H_{xk}\ne0\). Since \(H\) is monomial, its \(k\)-th column has no other nonzero entry, so
\[
 He_k=h e_x. \tag{4}
\]

First derive the hard-intervention response rather than identifying it with an observed quantity by definition. Under \(\operatorname{do}(V_x=t)\), the remaining equilibrium equations are
\[
 Q_{-x,-x}V_{-x}=H_{-x,:}\xi^{\mathcal M}-Q_{-x,x}t.
\]
The postintervention determinant condition permits inversion and differentiation, giving
\[
 \frac{\partial\,\operatorname{Eq}_{\mathcal M}(V_{-x}\mid\operatorname{do}(V_x=t))}{\partial t}
 =-Q_{-x,-x}^{-1}Q_{-x,x}. \tag{5}
\]
The cofactor formula and the two determinant conditions give
\[
 (Q^{-1})_{xx}=\frac{\det(Q_{-x,-x})}{\det(Q)}\ne0. \tag{6}
\]
Taking the rows other than \(x\) in \(QQ^{-1}e_x=e_x\) yields
\[
 Q_{-x,-x}(Q^{-1})_{-x,x}+Q_{-x,x}(Q^{-1})_{xx}=0.
\]
Division is legal by (6), and comparison with (5) proves
\[
 \boldsymbol\theta_{\leftarrow x}(\mathcal M)
 =\frac{(Q^{-1})_{-x,x}}{(Q^{-1})_{xx}}. \tag{7}
\]

Set \(T=Q^{-1}H\), so \(T\) is invertible and \(A=T_{\mathsf O,:}\). Equation (4) implies
\[
 T_{:,k}=h(Q^{-1})_{:,x}. \tag{8}
\]
In particular, (6) and \(h\ne0\) imply \(A_{xk}=h(Q^{-1})_{xx}\ne0\). Dividing the observed coordinates of (8) and using (7) gives the vector ratio, and taking coordinate \(y\) gives the scalar ratio.

It remains to prove the deletion rank. From (4), row \(k\) of \(H^{-1}\) is zero off column \(x\) and \((H^{-1})_{kx}=h^{-1}\). Therefore, using \(Q_{xx}=1\),
\[
 (T^{-1})_{kx}=(H^{-1}Q)_{kx}=h^{-1}Q_{xx}=h^{-1}\ne0. \tag{9}
\]
The inverse-cofactor formula applied to (9) shows \(\det(T_{-x,-k})\ne0\). Thus all rows of \(T_{-x,-k}\) are linearly independent. The \(p-1\) observed rows other than \(x\) form the submatrix \(A_{-x,-k}\), so those rows are independent and \(\operatorname{rank}(A_{-x,-k})=p-1\), as claimed.

added_lemmas.statement:
The set \(J_x(C)\) is nonempty. For every \(j\in J_x(C)\), \(\operatorname{Cert}(C,x)\) returns a canonical completion \(\mathcal M_j=(n,Q_j,H_j,\varepsilon)\in\mathfrak F_x(P_X)\) such that \(A^{\mathcal M_j}=C\), \(s_{\mathcal M_j}(x)=j\),
\[
 \boldsymbol\theta_{\leftarrow x}(\mathcal M_j)=\frac{C_{-x,j}}{C_{xj}},
 \qquad
 \theta_{y\leftarrow x}(\mathcal M_j)=\frac{C_{yj}}{C_{xj}}.
\]
All admissible indices and all these witnesses are computable in \(O(n^4)\) exact real-arithmetic operations. If \(C\) is rational, every returned \(Q_j\) and \(H_j\) is rational.
added_lemmas.proof_tex:
By full row rank, the \(p\) rows of \(C\) are independent. Extend them to the rows of a matrix \(T_0\in\operatorname{GL}_n(\mathbb R)\), preserving \((T_0)_{\mathsf O,:}=C\), and put \(W_0=T_0^{-1}\). The \((x,x)\)-entry of \(T_0W_0=I_n\) is
\[
 1=\sum_{j=1}^n C_{xj}(W_0)_{jx}. \tag{10}
\]
Thus some \(j\) has both \(C_{xj}\ne0\) and \((W_0)_{jx}\ne0\). The inverse-cofactor formula says that this latter inequality is equivalent to \(\det((T_0)_{-x,-j})\ne0\). Its \(p-1\) observed rows other than \(x\), namely the rows of \(C_{-x,-j}\), are therefore independent. Hence \(j\in J_x(C)\), proving nonemptiness.

Now fix any \(j\in J_x(C)\). We first justify the shear prescribed by \(\operatorname{Cert}\). Because the rows of \(C_{-x,:}\) are independent,
\[
 \operatorname{rank}(C_{-x,-j})<p-1
 \quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad
 e_j^\top\in\operatorname{rowspan}(C_{-x,:}). \tag{11}
\]
Indeed, a nonzero dependence after deletion gives a nonzero linear combination of the independent full rows supported only at coordinate \(j\), and hence a nonzero multiple of \(e_j^\top\); the converse follows by deleting coordinate \(j\). Row \(j\) of \(W_0\) is the unique coordinate vector of \(e_j^\top\) in the row basis of \(T_0\), since
\[
 e_j^\top=(e_j^\top W_0)T_0.
\]
Consequently (11) is also equivalent to
\[
 (W_0)_{jx}=0
 \quad\text{and}\quad
 (W_0)_{j\ell}=0\ \text{for every }\ell\in\mathsf L. \tag{12}
\]
The admissibility of \(j\) rules out (12). If \((W_0)_{jx}\ne0\), set \(T_j=T_0\) and \(W_j=W_0\). Otherwise (12) supplies \(\ell\in\mathsf L\) with \((W_0)_{j\ell}\ne0\). Since \(x\ne\ell\), the matrices \(I_n+e_\ell e_x^\top\) and \(I_n-e_\ell e_x^\top\) are inverse, so the prescribed shear satisfies
\[
 T_j=(I_n+e_\ell e_x^\top)T_0,
 \qquad
 W_j=W_0(I_n-e_\ell e_x^\top),
 \qquad
 (W_j)_{jx}=-(W_0)_{j\ell}\ne0. \tag{13}
\]
Only latent row \(\ell\) changes, hence \((T_j)_{\mathsf O,:}=C\), and \(T_j\) remains invertible.

Because \(T_j=W_j^{-1}\) and \((T_j)_{xj}=C_{xj}\ne0\), another inverse-cofactor identity gives
\[
 \det((W_j)_{-j,-x})\ne0. \tag{14}
\]
The determinant expansion in (14) contains a nonzero product. Its indices give a perfect matching from the source rows other than \(j\) to the equation columns other than \(x\). Augment it by assigning row \(j\) to column \(x\), and let \(\Pi_j\) permute the rows of \(W_j\) so that every diagonal entry of \(\Pi_jW_j\) is nonzero and row \(x\) is the old row \(j\). Set
\[
 D_j=\operatorname{diag}(\Pi_jW_j),
 \qquad Q_j=D_j^{-1}\Pi_jW_j,
 \qquad H_j=D_j^{-1}\Pi_j. \tag{15}
\]
Then \(D_j\) is invertible, \(Q_j\) is invertible with unit diagonal, and \(H_j\) is monomial. Moreover,
\[
 Q_j^{-1}H_j
 =W_j^{-1}\Pi_j^{-1}D_jD_j^{-1}\Pi_j
 =T_j, \tag{16}
\]
so \([Q_j^{-1}H_j]_{\mathsf O,:}=C\) and \(\mathcal L(C\varepsilon)=P_X\). The canonical sources \(\varepsilon_1,\ldots,\varepsilon_n\) are mutually independent, nonconstant, and non-Gaussian by the population assumptions, while the columns of \(C\) are nonzero and pairwise nonproportional. Thus all irreducible LiNG and observed-law requirements in the definition of \(\mathfrak F_x(P_X)\) hold.

The augmentation in (15) gives \((H_j)_{xj}\ne0\), so \(s_{\mathcal M_j}(x)=j\). From (16),
\[
 C_{xj}=(Q_j^{-1})_{xx}(H_j)_{xj}.
\]
Both \(C_{xj}\) and \((H_j)_{xj}\) are nonzero; hence \((Q_j^{-1})_{xx}\ne0\). The cofactor formula and invertibility of \(Q_j\) now give \(\det((Q_j)_{-x,-x})\ne0\). Therefore \(\mathcal M_j=(n,Q_j,H_j,\varepsilon)\) belongs to \(\mathfrak F_x(P_X)\). Applying the law-fiber response-rank lemma to this completion and using (16) proves both displayed response formulas.

For the operation count, Gaussian elimination extends the row basis and inverts \(T_0\) in \(O(n^3)\) arithmetic operations. Equivalence (12) classifies every deletion rank by scanning \(W_0\), in \(O(n^2)\) operations after the inverse. Each of at most \(n\) witnesses uses one \(O(n^2)\) shear, at most \(n\) augmenting-path searches each scanning at most \(n^2\) potential matching edges, and \(O(n^2)\) row normalization. Hence all witnesses require \(O(n^4)\) operations. This count uses exact zero tests in the real-arithmetic model; it is not a floating-point or bit-complexity statement. If \(C\) is rational, Gaussian elimination can choose a rational row-basis extension, and inversion, the integral shear, permutation, and divisions by the nonzero rational diagonal entries in (15) preserve rationality.

prose_updates.tldr: An observational law \(P_X\) with one normalized irreducible overcomplete-ICA representation \(X=C\varepsilon\) can support many cyclic latent LiNG mechanisms, but published irreducible-ICA uniqueness fixes their source count and mixing directions up to permutation and scaling. Over the full observational-law fiber of source-minimal one-shock-per-equation completions, the sharp response to one hard intervention is exactly the finite vector set \(\mathcal R_x^{\mathrm{vec}}(C)\); every scalar frontier is a coordinate projection. A latent-row shear and perfect matching construct an exact canonical same-law witness for every point in \(O(n^4)\) arithmetic operations. The separated iid layer supplies simultaneous uncertainty for this finite frontier, while the fourteen-stock Hong Kong series remains a population-level consumer unless dependent-time-series assumptions and empirical margins are separately certified.

project_justification.gap: Published irreducible-ICA results identify the source count and directions of an observational law up to permutation and scaling, and published latent cyclic LiNG work characterizes graph-level distributional equivalence or coefficients in specified graph classes. None characterizes the exact one-intervention response-vector image of every irreducible source-minimal completion of one numerical observational law.
project_justification.niche: Law-level ICA uniqueness makes deletion ranks and column ratios representation invariant, so a query-specific causal projection can be exact and far smaller than the compatible graph class without imposing dynamical stability.

sampling_model.design: Population identification conditions on the observational law \(P_X=\mathcal L(C\varepsilon)\) and ranges over every irreducible source-minimal one-shock-per-equation completion that entails that law and is solvable observationally and after intervention on \(x\). The inference layer uses observational iid sampling under \(P_X^{\otimes N}\) on the declared separated cumulant subclass.
sampling_model.units: \(N\) independent copies of the observed vector \(X\) under \(P_X^{\otimes N}\) for inference; no sampling condition is needed for the population law-fiber theorem.
sampling_model.treatment: A hard intervention replaces the structural equation for observed coordinate \(x\) by \(V_x=t\); the target is the joint response of all other observed coordinates to this one intervention, not a collection of jointly performed interventions.
sampling_model.overlap: Treatment-propensity overlap is not applicable. Population identification uses nonzero selected treatment loadings and deletion rank; uniform inference additionally uses the declared loading, minor, tensor, and separation margins.
sampling_model.nuisance_estimation: A normalized representative \(C\) is recovered up to column permutation and scaling from the observational law; the response-vector and scalar frontier maps are invariant to those indeterminacies. The separated iid construction estimates one common set of source directions, preserving the common source index across outcome coordinates.

prose_updates.related_work: ErikssonKoivunen2004 Theorem 3 is the primary all-non-Gaussian ICA identifiability result; DaiAlbrechtSpirtesZhang2026 Appendix B.1, Lemma 11 restates it for two irreducible representations as equality of source counts and mutual proportionality of mixing columns, and WangSeigal2026 records the same all-non-Gaussian no-collinear-columns criterion while developing the broader OICA benchmark. Those results supply law-level direction uniqueness, not the causal query projection. DaiAlbrechtSpirtesZhang2026 otherwise characterizes graph-indexed distribution families by children bases and perfect matchings; the present result instead maps every numerical same-law completion to a one-intervention response-vector frontier and constructs a full mechanism for every point. TramontanoKivvaSalehkaleybarDrtonKiyavash2024 gives complete acyclic graphical effect criteria, while TramontanoDrtonEtesami2026 gives partial cyclic coefficient criteria for known mixed graphs. LacerdaSpirtesRamseyHoyer2008 constructs square row-permutation candidates and distribution-entailment classes, but does not impose solvability after a selected intervention. BongersForrePetersMooij2021 supplies the distinction between observational and interventional solvability. The new contribution is the deletion-rank response image, its representation invariance, and exact canonical witnesses; published full-law ICA uniqueness is used as an antecedent.
prose_updates.technical_internal_limitation: The law fiber is deliberately restricted to irreducible source-minimal LiNG representations: every structural equation receives one distinct independent disturbance, and every observed mixing column is nonzero and pairwise nonproportional. Reducible representations, source splitting, duplicated or proportional directions, and extra shocks are excluded because they can change both source count and the causal frontier. This is the precise boundary of the law-invariance claim; it is not a claim over the larger graphically irreducible fiber at exceptional coefficients. No dynamical stability restriction is imposed. The vector set concerns all observed responses to one intervention with a common source witness, not Cartesian products across outcomes and not joint multiple interventions. Uniform root-\(N\) inference still requires denominator, minor, tensor, and separation margins. The fourteen-stock Hong Kong series is a population-certificate consumer only until serial dependence, mechanism changes, and empirical separation are addressed by a separate theorem and data certificate.
prose_updates.honest_scope: The population theorem covers the full observational-law fiber of irreducible source-minimal one-shock-per-equation cyclic LiNG completions with invertible observational and \(x\)-postintervention systems. It proves the finite response-vector frontier, all scalar coordinate projections, exact same-law witnesses, point-identification tests, and \(O(n^4)\) exact real-arithmetic certification without stability. Published irreducible-ICA uniqueness supplies the equality of source counts and directions up to permutation and scaling; only the law-conditioned causal deletion-rank projection and witness construction are new. Reducible, split-source, duplicated-direction, or proportional-column representations are outside scope, as are stability-refined fibers, Cartesian cross-outcome recombinations, joint multiple interventions, and dependent-time-series inference for the Hong Kong data. The separated iid inference results apply only on their explicit cumulant, loading, minor, and denominator margins.

proofs.proof_tex:
Define the causal response-set target by the left side of (17); it ranges over structural mechanisms and is not defined to equal an observed-law functional. We prove its equality with the computable deletion-rank map on the right.

The canonical law-fiber witness lemma first gives \(J_x(C)\ne\varnothing\). For the necessity inclusion, fix an arbitrary \(\mathcal M\in\mathfrak F_x(P_X)\). By the cited irreducible-ICA law-uniqueness lemma, \(m_{\mathcal M}=n\) and
\[
 A^{\mathcal M}=C\Pi D \tag{19}
\]
for a permutation matrix \(\Pi\) and an invertible diagonal matrix \(D\). Write \(\Pi e_k=e_{\pi(k)}\), and let \(k=s_{\mathcal M}(x)\). The law-fiber response-rank lemma gives
\[
 A^{\mathcal M}_{xk}\ne0,
 \qquad \operatorname{rank}(A^{\mathcal M}_{-x,-k})=p-1,
 \qquad
 \boldsymbol\theta_{\leftarrow x}(\mathcal M)
 =\frac{A^{\mathcal M}_{-x,k}}{A^{\mathcal M}_{xk}}. \tag{20}
\]
The monomial-frontier invariance lemma applied to (19) turns (20) into
\[
 \pi(k)\in J_x(C),
 \qquad
 \boldsymbol\theta_{\leftarrow x}(\mathcal M)
 =\frac{C_{-x,\pi(k)}}{C_{x,\pi(k)}}
 \in\mathcal R_x^{\mathrm{vec}}(C). \tag{21}
\]
This proves the inclusion of the causal target in the observable functional for every completion of the observational law, not merely for a fixed source tuple.

For sufficiency, take any \(r\in\mathcal R_x^{\mathrm{vec}}(C)\). By definition, \(r=C_{-x,j}/C_{xj}\) for some \(j\in J_x(C)\). The canonical witness lemma constructs
\[
 \mathcal M_j=(n,Q_j,H_j,\varepsilon)\in\mathfrak F_x(P_X),
 \qquad A^{\mathcal M_j}=C,
 \qquad
 \boldsymbol\theta_{\leftarrow x}(\mathcal M_j)=r. \tag{22}
\]
Thus every value of the observable deletion-rank map is attained by a full structural completion having exactly the canonical representation. Equations (21)--(22) prove (17) and its sharpness over the whole law fiber.

For any completion, the definition of the scalar hard-intervention effect and the response-rank lemma give
\[
 \theta_{y\leftarrow x}(\mathcal M)
 =\operatorname{pr}_y\boldsymbol\theta_{\leftarrow x}(\mathcal M).
\]
Projecting both sides of (17) coordinatewise therefore proves (18); in particular, no Cartesian combination of effects from different source indices is introduced.

If distinct \(j,k\in J_x(C)\) had equal vector ratios, adjoining their common treatment coordinate \(1\) would give
\[
 \frac{C_{:,j}}{C_{xj}}=\frac{C_{:,k}}{C_{xk}}.
\]
Because both denominators are nonzero, this would make columns \(c_j\) and \(c_k\) proportional, contrary to the distinct-directions assumption. Hence the index-to-vector map is injective. Since \(J_x(C)\) is nonempty, the vector target is a singleton exactly when \(|J_x(C)|=1\).

For the scalar claim, the row of \(C_{\{x,y\},J_x(C)}\) indexed by \(x\) is nonzero entrywise. This two-row matrix has rank one if and only if
\[
 C_{xj}C_{yk}-C_{xk}C_{yj}=0
 \quad\text{for all }j,k\in J_x(C). \tag{23}
\]
Division by \(C_{xj}C_{xk}\ne0\) shows that (23) is equivalent to equality of all ratios \(C_{yj}/C_{xj}\), hence to \(|\mathcal R_{xy}(C)|=1\). By (18), this is exactly scalar point identification over the law fiber.

Finally, the canonical witness lemma computes every admissible index and its exact completion in \(O(n^4)\) operations and preserves rationality. The vector and scalar ratios require only \(O(pn)\) additional arithmetic, and selecting one index for each repeated scalar ratio cannot increase the bound. This proves the stated certificate and complexity conclusions.

added_lemmas.statement:
Let \(\widetilde C=C\Pi D\), where \(\Pi e_k=e_{\pi(k)}\) for a permutation \(\pi\) of \(\mathsf S\) and \(D=\operatorname{diag}(d_1,\ldots,d_n)\) with every \(d_k\ne0\). Then \(k\in J_x(\widetilde C)\) if and only if \(\pi(k)\in J_x(C)\), and for every such \(k\),
\[
 \frac{\widetilde C_{-x,k}}{\widetilde C_{xk}}
 =\frac{C_{-x,\pi(k)}}{C_{x,\pi(k)}}.
\]
Consequently \(\mathcal R_x^{\mathrm{vec}}(\widetilde C)=\mathcal R_x^{\mathrm{vec}}(C)\) and \(\mathcal R_{xy}(\widetilde C)=\mathcal R_{xy}(C)\) for every \(y\in\mathsf O\setminus\{x\}\).
added_lemmas.proof_tex:
By the convention \(\Pi e_k=e_{\pi(k)}\), the \(k\)-th column of \(\widetilde C\) is
\[
 \widetilde C_{:,k}=d_k C_{:,\pi(k)}. \tag{1}
\]
Since \(d_k\ne0\), equation (1) gives
\[
 \widetilde C_{xk}\ne0
 \quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad
 C_{x,\pi(k)}\ne0. \tag{2}
\]
After deleting column \(k\), the remaining columns of \(\widetilde C_{-x,-k}\) are obtained from those of \(C_{-x,-\pi(k)}\) by a column permutation and multiplication by a nonsingular diagonal matrix. Both operations preserve row rank, and hence
\[
 \operatorname{rank}(\widetilde C_{-x,-k})
 =\operatorname{rank}(C_{-x,-\pi(k)}). \tag{3}
\]
Equations (2)--(3) and the definition of \(J_x\) prove the membership equivalence. Dividing the \((-x)\)-coordinates of (1) by its \(x\)-coordinate cancels \(d_k\) and proves the displayed response-ratio identity. Because \(\pi\) is bijective, taking the images of the two admissible-index sets gives equality of the vector frontiers. Taking coordinate \(y\) gives equality of the scalar frontiers by their definitions.

added_lemmas.statement:
For every \(\mathcal M=(m_{\mathcal M},Q,H,\xi^{\mathcal M})\in\mathfrak F_x(P_X)\), put \(A=A^{\mathcal M}\) and \(k=s_{\mathcal M}(x)\). Then
\[
 A_{xk}\ne0,
 \qquad \operatorname{rank}(A_{-x,-k})=p-1,
 \qquad \boldsymbol\theta_{\leftarrow x}(\mathcal M)=\frac{A_{-x,k}}{A_{xk}},
 \qquad \theta_{y\leftarrow x}(\mathcal M)=\frac{A_{yk}}{A_{xk}}.
\]
added_lemmas.proof_tex:
Fix \(\mathcal M\) in the stated fiber and abbreviate \(m=m_{\mathcal M}\). Membership in \(\mathfrak F_x(P_X)\) gives \(Q_{ii}=1\), monomial \(H\), \(\det(Q)\ne0\), and \(\det(Q_{-x,-x})\ne0\). Let \(k=s_{\mathcal M}(x)\) and \(h=H_{xk}\ne0\). Since \(H\) is monomial, its \(k\)-th column has no other nonzero entry, so
\[
 He_k=h e_x. \tag{4}
\]

First derive the hard-intervention response rather than identifying it with an observed quantity by definition. Under \(\operatorname{do}(V_x=t)\), the remaining equilibrium equations are
\[
 Q_{-x,-x}V_{-x}=H_{-x,:}\xi^{\mathcal M}-Q_{-x,x}t.
\]
The postintervention determinant condition permits inversion and differentiation, giving
\[
 \frac{\partial\,\operatorname{Eq}_{\mathcal M}(V_{-x}\mid\operatorname{do}(V_x=t))}{\partial t}
 =-Q_{-x,-x}^{-1}Q_{-x,x}. \tag{5}
\]
The cofactor formula and the two determinant conditions give
\[
 (Q^{-1})_{xx}=\frac{\det(Q_{-x,-x})}{\det(Q)}\ne0. \tag{6}
\]
Taking the rows other than \(x\) in \(QQ^{-1}e_x=e_x\) yields
\[
 Q_{-x,-x}(Q^{-1})_{-x,x}+Q_{-x,x}(Q^{-1})_{xx}=0.
\]
Division is legal by (6), and comparison with (5) proves
\[
 \boldsymbol\theta_{\leftarrow x}(\mathcal M)
 =\frac{(Q^{-1})_{-x,x}}{(Q^{-1})_{xx}}. \tag{7}
\]

Set \(T=Q^{-1}H\), so \(T\) is invertible and \(A=T_{\mathsf O,:}\). Equation (4) implies
\[
 T_{:,k}=h(Q^{-1})_{:,x}. \tag{8}
\]
In particular, (6) and \(h\ne0\) imply \(A_{xk}=h(Q^{-1})_{xx}\ne0\). Dividing the observed coordinates of (8) and using (7) gives the vector ratio, and taking coordinate \(y\) gives the scalar ratio.

It remains to prove the deletion rank. From (4), row \(k\) of \(H^{-1}\) is zero off column \(x\) and \((H^{-1})_{kx}=h^{-1}\). Therefore, using \(Q_{xx}=1\),
\[
 (T^{-1})_{kx}=(H^{-1}Q)_{kx}=h^{-1}Q_{xx}=h^{-1}\ne0. \tag{9}
\]
The inverse-cofactor formula applied to (9) shows \(\det(T_{-x,-k})\ne0\). Thus all rows of \(T_{-x,-k}\) are linearly independent. The \(p-1\) observed rows other than \(x\) form the submatrix \(A_{-x,-k}\), so those rows are independent and \(\operatorname{rank}(A_{-x,-k})=p-1\), as claimed.

added_lemmas.statement:
The set \(J_x(C)\) is nonempty. For every \(j\in J_x(C)\), \(\operatorname{Cert}(C,x)\) returns a canonical completion \(\mathcal M_j=(n,Q_j,H_j,\varepsilon)\in\mathfrak F_x(P_X)\) such that \(A^{\mathcal M_j}=C\), \(s_{\mathcal M_j}(x)=j\),
\[
 \boldsymbol\theta_{\leftarrow x}(\mathcal M_j)=\frac{C_{-x,j}}{C_{xj}},
 \qquad
 \theta_{y\leftarrow x}(\mathcal M_j)=\frac{C_{yj}}{C_{xj}}.
\]
All admissible indices and all these witnesses are computable in \(O(n^4)\) exact real-arithmetic operations. If \(C\) is rational, every returned \(Q_j\) and \(H_j\) is rational.
added_lemmas.proof_tex:
By full row rank, the \(p\) rows of \(C\) are independent. Extend them to the rows of a matrix \(T_0\in\operatorname{GL}_n(\mathbb R)\), preserving \((T_0)_{\mathsf O,:}=C\), and put \(W_0=T_0^{-1}\). The \((x,x)\)-entry of \(T_0W_0=I_n\) is
\[
 1=\sum_{j=1}^n C_{xj}(W_0)_{jx}. \tag{10}
\]
Thus some \(j\) has both \(C_{xj}\ne0\) and \((W_0)_{jx}\ne0\). The inverse-cofactor formula says that this latter inequality is equivalent to \(\det((T_0)_{-x,-j})\ne0\). Its \(p-1\) observed rows other than \(x\), namely the rows of \(C_{-x,-j}\), are therefore independent. Hence \(j\in J_x(C)\), proving nonemptiness.

Now fix any \(j\in J_x(C)\). We first justify the shear prescribed by \(\operatorname{Cert}\). Because the rows of \(C_{-x,:}\) are independent,
\[
 \operatorname{rank}(C_{-x,-j})<p-1
 \quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad
 e_j^\top\in\operatorname{rowspan}(C_{-x,:}). \tag{11}
\]
Indeed, a nonzero dependence after deletion gives a nonzero linear combination of the independent full rows supported only at coordinate \(j\), and hence a nonzero multiple of \(e_j^\top\); the converse follows by deleting coordinate \(j\). Row \(j\) of \(W_0\) is the unique coordinate vector of \(e_j^\top\) in the row basis of \(T_0\), since
\[
 e_j^\top=(e_j^\top W_0)T_0.
\]
Consequently (11) is also equivalent to
\[
 (W_0)_{jx}=0
 \quad\text{and}\quad
 (W_0)_{j\ell}=0\ \text{for every }\ell\in\mathsf L. \tag{12}
\]
The admissibility of \(j\) rules out (12). If \((W_0)_{jx}\ne0\), set \(T_j=T_0\) and \(W_j=W_0\). Otherwise (12) supplies \(\ell\in\mathsf L\) with \((W_0)_{j\ell}\ne0\). Since \(x\ne\ell\), the matrices \(I_n+e_\ell e_x^\top\) and \(I_n-e_\ell e_x^\top\) are inverse, so the prescribed shear satisfies
\[
 T_j=(I_n+e_\ell e_x^\top)T_0,
 \qquad
 W_j=W_0(I_n-e_\ell e_x^\top),
 \qquad
 (W_j)_{jx}=-(W_0)_{j\ell}\ne0. \tag{13}
\]
Only latent row \(\ell\) changes, hence \((T_j)_{\mathsf O,:}=C\), and \(T_j\) remains invertible.

Because \(T_j=W_j^{-1}\) and \((T_j)_{xj}=C_{xj}\ne0\), another inverse-cofactor identity gives
\[
 \det((W_j)_{-j,-x})\ne0. \tag{14}
\]
The determinant expansion in (14) contains a nonzero product. Its indices give a perfect matching from the source rows other than \(j\) to the equation columns other than \(x\). Augment it by assigning row \(j\) to column \(x\), and let \(\Pi_j\) permute the rows of \(W_j\) so that every diagonal entry of \(\Pi_jW_j\) is nonzero and row \(x\) is the old row \(j\). Set
\[
 D_j=\operatorname{diag}(\Pi_jW_j),
 \qquad Q_j=D_j^{-1}\Pi_jW_j,
 \qquad H_j=D_j^{-1}\Pi_j. \tag{15}
\]
Then \(D_j\) is invertible, \(Q_j\) is invertible with unit diagonal, and \(H_j\) is monomial. Moreover,
\[
 Q_j^{-1}H_j
 =W_j^{-1}\Pi_j^{-1}D_jD_j^{-1}\Pi_j
 =T_j, \tag{16}
\]
so \([Q_j^{-1}H_j]_{\mathsf O,:}=C\) and \(\mathcal L(C\varepsilon)=P_X\). The canonical sources \(\varepsilon_1,\ldots,\varepsilon_n\) are mutually independent, nonconstant, and non-Gaussian by the population assumptions, while the columns of \(C\) are nonzero and pairwise nonproportional. Thus all irreducible LiNG and observed-law requirements in the definition of \(\mathfrak F_x(P_X)\) hold.

The augmentation in (15) gives \((H_j)_{xj}\ne0\), so \(s_{\mathcal M_j}(x)=j\). From (16),
\[
 C_{xj}=(Q_j^{-1})_{xx}(H_j)_{xj}.
\]
Both \(C_{xj}\) and \((H_j)_{xj}\) are nonzero; hence \((Q_j^{-1})_{xx}\ne0\). The cofactor formula and invertibility of \(Q_j\) now give \(\det((Q_j)_{-x,-x})\ne0\). Therefore \(\mathcal M_j=(n,Q_j,H_j,\varepsilon)\) belongs to \(\mathfrak F_x(P_X)\). Applying the law-fiber response-rank lemma to this completion and using (16) proves both displayed response formulas.

For the operation count, Gaussian elimination extends the row basis and inverts \(T_0\) in \(O(n^3)\) arithmetic operations. Equivalence (12) classifies every deletion rank by scanning \(W_0\), in \(O(n^2)\) operations after the inverse. Each of at most \(n\) witnesses uses one \(O(n^2)\) shear, at most \(n\) augmenting-path searches each scanning at most \(n^2\) potential matching edges, and \(O(n^2)\) row normalization. Hence all witnesses require \(O(n^4)\) operations. This count uses exact zero tests in the real-arithmetic model; it is not a floating-point or bit-complexity statement. If \(C\) is rational, Gaussian elimination can choose a rational row-basis extension, and inversion, the integral shear, permutation, and divisions by the nonzero rational diagonal entries in (15) preserve rationality.

proposed.comparator_claim: Section 4 constructs square candidates by admissible row permutation and row normalization, while Theorem 1 states distribution-entailment equivalence of the LiNG-D output; it does not assert solvability after a specified intervention.
The main equivalence theorem characterizes equality of graph-indexed observed distribution families by children-basis and perfect-matching conditions.

Theorem 3 gives identifiability of a linear ICA mixing system when all sources are non-Gaussian, including the overcomplete case; Dai et al., Appendix B.1, Lemma 11 states the irreducible equal-count and mutual-proportionality form used here.
The total-effect theorem gives a complete graphical criterion for generic effect identification in acyclic latent-variable LiNGAM.
The cyclic section gives a necessary coefficient-identification condition in general and a complete result for restricted cycle structures.
Section 1 records the all-non-Gaussian overcomplete-ICA identifiability criterion that no two mixing columns are collinear, crediting Eriksson and Koivunen Theorem 3.
Theorem 4a gives essential uniqueness of a three-factor tensor decomposition under the Kruskal-rank inequality.
The paper develops robust tensor-decomposition methods under quantitative nondegeneracy conditions.
The finite-cumulant-sequence theorem implies that a nondegenerate non-Gaussian law with all moments has infinitely many nonzero higher cumulants.

proposed_core_edits.reason: The table must record that published full-law irreducible ICA uniqueness is an exact antecedent, while the deletion-rank causal projection and witnesses are the new tightening.

prose_updates.tldr: An observational law \(P_X\) with one normalized irreducible overcomplete-ICA representation \(X=C\varepsilon\) can support many cyclic latent LiNG mechanisms, but published irreducible-ICA uniqueness fixes their source count and mixing directions up to permutation and scaling. Over the full observational-law fiber of source-minimal one-shock-per-equation completions, the sharp response to one hard intervention is exactly the finite vector set \(\mathcal R_x^{\mathrm{vec}}(C)\); every scalar frontier is a coordinate projection. A latent-row shear and perfect matching construct an exact canonical same-law witness for every point in \(O(n^4)\) arithmetic operations. The separated iid layer supplies simultaneous uncertainty for this finite frontier, while the fourteen-stock Hong Kong series remains a population-level consumer unless dependent-time-series assumptions and empirical margins are separately certified.

project_justification.gap: Published irreducible-ICA results identify the source count and directions of an observational law up to permutation and scaling, and published latent cyclic LiNG work characterizes graph-level distributional equivalence or coefficients in specified graph classes. None characterizes the exact one-intervention response-vector image of every irreducible source-minimal completion of one numerical observational law.
project_justification.niche: Law-level ICA uniqueness makes deletion ranks and column ratios representation invariant, so a query-specific causal projection can be exact and far smaller than the compatible graph class without imposing dynamical stability.
project_justification.fill: The paper proves the sharp response-vector frontier, its scalar coordinate projections, exact canonical witnesses, vector and scalar point-identification certificates, polynomial-time enumeration, and a separated iid uncertainty layer.

sampling_model.design: Population identification conditions on the observational law \(P_X=\mathcal L(C\varepsilon)\) and ranges over every irreducible source-minimal one-shock-per-equation completion that entails that law and is solvable observationally and after intervention on \(x\). The inference layer uses observational iid sampling under \(P_X^{\otimes N}\) on the declared separated cumulant subclass.
sampling_model.units: \(N\) independent copies of the observed vector \(X\) under \(P_X^{\otimes N}\) for inference; no sampling condition is needed for the population law-fiber theorem.
sampling_model.treatment: A hard intervention replaces the structural equation for observed coordinate \(x\) by \(V_x=t\); the target is the joint response of all other observed coordinates to this one intervention, not a collection of jointly performed interventions.
sampling_model.overlap: Treatment-propensity overlap is not applicable. Population identification uses nonzero selected treatment loadings and deletion rank; uniform inference additionally uses the declared loading, minor, tensor, and separation margins.
sampling_model.nuisance_estimation: A normalized representative \(C\) is recovered up to column permutation and scaling from the observational law; the response-vector and scalar frontier maps are invariant to those indeterminacies. The separated iid construction estimates one common set of source directions, preserving the common source index across outcome coordinates.

prose_updates.related_work: ErikssonKoivunen2004 Theorem 3 is the primary all-non-Gaussian ICA identifiability result; DaiAlbrechtSpirtesZhang2026 Appendix B.1, Lemma 11 restates it for two irreducible representations as equality of source counts and mutual proportionality of mixing columns, and WangSeigal2026 records the same all-non-Gaussian no-collinear-columns criterion while developing the broader OICA benchmark. Those results supply law-level direction uniqueness, not the causal query projection. DaiAlbrechtSpirtesZhang2026 otherwise characterizes graph-indexed distribution families by children bases and perfect matchings; the present result instead maps every numerical same-law completion to a one-intervention response-vector frontier and constructs a full mechanism for every point. TramontanoKivvaSalehkaleybarDrtonKiyavash2024 gives complete acyclic graphical effect criteria, while TramontanoDrtonEtesami2026 gives partial cyclic coefficient criteria for known mixed graphs. LacerdaSpirtesRamseyHoyer2008 constructs square row-permutation candidates and distribution-entailment classes, but does not impose solvability after a selected intervention. BongersForrePetersMooij2021 supplies the distinction between observational and interventional solvability. The new contribution is the deletion-rank response image, its representation invariance, and exact canonical witnesses; published full-law ICA uniqueness is used as an antecedent.
prose_updates.technical_internal_limitation: The law fiber is deliberately restricted to irreducible source-minimal LiNG representations: every structural equation receives one distinct independent disturbance, and every observed mixing column is nonzero and pairwise nonproportional. Reducible representations, source splitting, duplicated or proportional directions, and extra shocks are excluded because they can change both source count and the causal frontier. This is the precise boundary of the law-invariance claim; it is not a claim over the larger graphically irreducible fiber at exceptional coefficients. No dynamical stability restriction is imposed. The vector set concerns all observed responses to one intervention with a common source witness, not Cartesian products across outcomes and not joint multiple interventions. Uniform root-\(N\) inference still requires denominator, minor, tensor, and separation margins. The fourteen-stock Hong Kong series is a population-certificate consumer only until serial dependence, mechanism changes, and empirical separation are addressed by a separate theorem and data certificate.
prose_updates.honest_scope: The population theorem covers the full observational-law fiber of irreducible source-minimal one-shock-per-equation cyclic LiNG completions with invertible observational and \(x\)-postintervention systems. It proves the finite response-vector frontier, all scalar coordinate projections, exact same-law witnesses, point-identification tests, and \(O(n^4)\) exact real-arithmetic certification without stability. Published irreducible-ICA uniqueness supplies the equality of source counts and directions up to permutation and scaling; only the law-conditioned causal deletion-rank projection and witness construction are new. Reducible, split-source, duplicated-direction, or proportional-column representations are outside scope, as are stability-refined fibers, Cartesian cross-outcome recombinations, joint multiple interventions, and dependent-time-series inference for the Hong Kong data. The separated iid inference results apply only on their explicit cumulant, loading, minor, and denominator margins.

statement_notes.justification: The theorem replaces a large cyclic graph equivalence class by the exact response-vector image of every irreducible source-minimal completion of one observational law, with constructive sharpness.
statement_notes.gap: Published irreducible-ICA uniqueness identifies source directions up to permutation and scaling, while DaiAlbrechtSpirtesZhang2026 and TramontanoDrtonEtesami2026 study graph-family equivalence or coefficient criteria; none gives this query-specific deletion-rank image and exact causal witnesses.
statement_notes.consumer: For the fourteen-stock Hong Kong example of DaiAlbrechtSpirtesZhang2026, the population map compresses \(19{,}008\) compatible graphs into one finite response-vector set for a selected intervention, whose coordinates give all ordered stock responses without false Cartesian combinations.

proofs.proof_tex:
Define the causal response-set target by the left side of (17); it ranges over structural mechanisms and is not defined to equal an observed-law functional. We prove its equality with the computable deletion-rank map on the right.

The canonical law-fiber witness lemma first gives \(J_x(C)\ne\varnothing\). For the necessity inclusion, fix an arbitrary \(\mathcal M\in\mathfrak F_x(P_X)\). By the cited irreducible-ICA law-uniqueness lemma, \(m_{\mathcal M}=n\) and
\[
 A^{\mathcal M}=C\Pi D \tag{19}
\]
for a permutation matrix \(\Pi\) and an invertible diagonal matrix \(D\). Write \(\Pi e_k=e_{\pi(k)}\), and let \(k=s_{\mathcal M}(x)\). The law-fiber response-rank lemma gives
\[
 A^{\mathcal M}_{xk}\ne0,
 \qquad \operatorname{rank}(A^{\mathcal M}_{-x,-k})=p-1,
 \qquad
 \boldsymbol\theta_{\leftarrow x}(\mathcal M)
 =\frac{A^{\mathcal M}_{-x,k}}{A^{\mathcal M}_{xk}}. \tag{20}
\]
The monomial-frontier invariance lemma applied to (19) turns (20) into
\[
 \pi(k)\in J_x(C),
 \qquad
 \boldsymbol\theta_{\leftarrow x}(\mathcal M)
 =\frac{C_{-x,\pi(k)}}{C_{x,\pi(k)}}
 \in\mathcal R_x^{\mathrm{vec}}(C). \tag{21}
\]
This proves the inclusion of the causal target in the observable functional for every completion of the observational law, not merely for a fixed source tuple.

For sufficiency, take any \(r\in\mathcal R_x^{\mathrm{vec}}(C)\). By definition, \(r=C_{-x,j}/C_{xj}\) for some \(j\in J_x(C)\). The canonical witness lemma constructs
\[
 \mathcal M_j=(n,Q_j,H_j,\varepsilon)\in\mathfrak F_x(P_X),
 \qquad A^{\mathcal M_j}=C,
 \qquad
 \boldsymbol\theta_{\leftarrow x}(\mathcal M_j)=r. \tag{22}
\]
Thus every value of the observable deletion-rank map is attained by a full structural completion having exactly the canonical representation. Equations (21)--(22) prove (17) and its sharpness over the whole law fiber.

For any completion, the definition of the scalar hard-intervention effect and the response-rank lemma give
\[
 \theta_{y\leftarrow x}(\mathcal M)
 =\operatorname{pr}_y\boldsymbol\theta_{\leftarrow x}(\mathcal M).
\]
Projecting both sides of (17) coordinatewise therefore proves (18); in particular, no Cartesian combination of effects from different source indices is introduced.

If distinct \(j,k\in J_x(C)\) had equal vector ratios, adjoining their common treatment coordinate \(1\) would give
\[
 \frac{C_{:,j}}{C_{xj}}=\frac{C_{:,k}}{C_{xk}}.
\]
Because both denominators are nonzero, this would make columns \(c_j\) and \(c_k\) proportional, contrary to the distinct-directions assumption. Hence the index-to-vector map is injective. Since \(J_x(C)\) is nonempty, the vector target is a singleton exactly when \(|J_x(C)|=1\).

For the scalar claim, the row of \(C_{\{x,y\},J_x(C)}\) indexed by \(x\) is nonzero entrywise. This two-row matrix has rank one if and only if
\[
 C_{xj}C_{yk}-C_{xk}C_{yj}=0
 \quad\text{for all }j,k\in J_x(C). \tag{23}
\]
Division by \(C_{xj}C_{xk}\ne0\) shows that (23) is equivalent to equality of all ratios \(C_{yj}/C_{xj}\), hence to \(|\mathcal R_{xy}(C)|=1\). By (18), this is exactly scalar point identification over the law fiber.

Finally, the canonical witness lemma computes every admissible index and its exact completion in \(O(n^4)\) operations and preserves rationality. The vector and scalar ratios require only \(O(pn)\) additional arithmetic, and selecting one index for each repeated scalar ratio cannot increase the bound. This proves the stated certificate and complexity conclusions.

added_lemmas.statement: For every \(\mathcal M\in\mathfrak F_x(P_X)\), one has \(m_{\mathcal M}=n\), and there exist an \(n\)-by-\(n\) permutation matrix \(\Pi\) and an invertible diagonal matrix \(D\) such that \(A^{\mathcal M}=C\Pi D\).

added_lemmas.statement:
Let \(\widetilde C=C\Pi D\), where \(\Pi e_k=e_{\pi(k)}\) for a permutation \(\pi\) of \(\mathsf S\) and \(D=\operatorname{diag}(d_1,\ldots,d_n)\) with every \(d_k\ne0\). Then \(k\in J_x(\widetilde C)\) if and only if \(\pi(k)\in J_x(C)\), and for every such \(k\),
\[
 \frac{\widetilde C_{-x,k}}{\widetilde C_{xk}}
 =\frac{C_{-x,\pi(k)}}{C_{x,\pi(k)}}.
\]
Consequently \(\mathcal R_x^{\mathrm{vec}}(\widetilde C)=\mathcal R_x^{\mathrm{vec}}(C)\) and \(\mathcal R_{xy}(\widetilde C)=\mathcal R_{xy}(C)\) for every \(y\in\mathsf O\setminus\{x\}\).
added_lemmas.proof_tex:
By the convention \(\Pi e_k=e_{\pi(k)}\), the \(k\)-th column of \(\widetilde C\) is
\[
 \widetilde C_{:,k}=d_k C_{:,\pi(k)}. \tag{1}
\]
Since \(d_k\ne0\), equation (1) gives
\[
 \widetilde C_{xk}\ne0
 \quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad
 C_{x,\pi(k)}\ne0. \tag{2}
\]
After deleting column \(k\), the remaining columns of \(\widetilde C_{-x,-k}\) are obtained from those of \(C_{-x,-\pi(k)}\) by a column permutation and multiplication by a nonsingular diagonal matrix. Both operations preserve row rank, and hence
\[
 \operatorname{rank}(\widetilde C_{-x,-k})
 =\operatorname{rank}(C_{-x,-\pi(k)}). \tag{3}
\]
Equations (2)--(3) and the definition of \(J_x\) prove the membership equivalence. Dividing the \((-x)\)-coordinates of (1) by its \(x\)-coordinate cancels \(d_k\) and proves the displayed response-ratio identity. Because \(\pi\) is bijective, taking the images of the two admissible-index sets gives equality of the vector frontiers. Taking coordinate \(y\) gives equality of the scalar frontiers by their definitions.

added_lemmas.statement:
For every \(\mathcal M=(m_{\mathcal M},Q,H,\xi^{\mathcal M})\in\mathfrak F_x(P_X)\), put \(A=A^{\mathcal M}\) and \(k=s_{\mathcal M}(x)\). Then
\[
 A_{xk}\ne0,
 \qquad \operatorname{rank}(A_{-x,-k})=p-1,
 \qquad \boldsymbol\theta_{\leftarrow x}(\mathcal M)=\frac{A_{-x,k}}{A_{xk}},
 \qquad \theta_{y\leftarrow x}(\mathcal M)=\frac{A_{yk}}{A_{xk}}.
\]
added_lemmas.proof_tex:
Fix \(\mathcal M\) in the stated fiber and abbreviate \(m=m_{\mathcal M}\). Membership in \(\mathfrak F_x(P_X)\) gives \(Q_{ii}=1\), monomial \(H\), \(\det(Q)\ne0\), and \(\det(Q_{-x,-x})\ne0\). Let \(k=s_{\mathcal M}(x)\) and \(h=H_{xk}\ne0\). Since \(H\) is monomial, its \(k\)-th column has no other nonzero entry, so
\[
 He_k=h e_x. \tag{4}
\]

First derive the hard-intervention response rather than identifying it with an observed quantity by definition. Under \(\operatorname{do}(V_x=t)\), the remaining equilibrium equations are
\[
 Q_{-x,-x}V_{-x}=H_{-x,:}\xi^{\mathcal M}-Q_{-x,x}t.
\]
The postintervention determinant condition permits inversion and differentiation, giving
\[
 \frac{\partial\,\operatorname{Eq}_{\mathcal M}(V_{-x}\mid\operatorname{do}(V_x=t))}{\partial t}
 =-Q_{-x,-x}^{-1}Q_{-x,x}. \tag{5}
\]
The cofactor formula and the two determinant conditions give
\[
 (Q^{-1})_{xx}=\frac{\det(Q_{-x,-x})}{\det(Q)}\ne0. \tag{6}
\]
Taking the rows other than \(x\) in \(QQ^{-1}e_x=e_x\) yields
\[
 Q_{-x,-x}(Q^{-1})_{-x,x}+Q_{-x,x}(Q^{-1})_{xx}=0.
\]
Division is legal by (6), and comparison with (5) proves
\[
 \boldsymbol\theta_{\leftarrow x}(\mathcal M)
 =\frac{(Q^{-1})_{-x,x}}{(Q^{-1})_{xx}}. \tag{7}
\]

Set \(T=Q^{-1}H\), so \(T\) is invertible and \(A=T_{\mathsf O,:}\). Equation (4) implies
\[
 T_{:,k}=h(Q^{-1})_{:,x}. \tag{8}
\]
In particular, (6) and \(h\ne0\) imply \(A_{xk}=h(Q^{-1})_{xx}\ne0\). Dividing the observed coordinates of (8) and using (7) gives the vector ratio, and taking coordinate \(y\) gives the scalar ratio.

It remains to prove the deletion rank. From (4), row \(k\) of \(H^{-1}\) is zero off column \(x\) and \((H^{-1})_{kx}=h^{-1}\). Therefore, using \(Q_{xx}=1\),
\[
 (T^{-1})_{kx}=(H^{-1}Q)_{kx}=h^{-1}Q_{xx}=h^{-1}\ne0. \tag{9}
\]
The inverse-cofactor formula applied to (9) shows \(\det(T_{-x,-k})\ne0\). Thus all rows of \(T_{-x,-k}\) are linearly independent. The \(p-1\) observed rows other than \(x\) form the submatrix \(A_{-x,-k}\), so those rows are independent and \(\operatorname{rank}(A_{-x,-k})=p-1\), as claimed.

added_lemmas.statement:
The set \(J_x(C)\) is nonempty. For every \(j\in J_x(C)\), \(\operatorname{Cert}(C,x)\) returns a canonical completion \(\mathcal M_j=(n,Q_j,H_j,\varepsilon)\in\mathfrak F_x(P_X)\) such that \(A^{\mathcal M_j}=C\), \(s_{\mathcal M_j}(x)=j\),
\[
 \boldsymbol\theta_{\leftarrow x}(\mathcal M_j)=\frac{C_{-x,j}}{C_{xj}},
 \qquad
 \theta_{y\leftarrow x}(\mathcal M_j)=\frac{C_{yj}}{C_{xj}}.
\]
All admissible indices and all these witnesses are computable in \(O(n^4)\) exact real-arithmetic operations. If \(C\) is rational, every returned \(Q_j\) and \(H_j\) is rational.
added_lemmas.proof_tex:
By full row rank, the \(p\) rows of \(C\) are independent. Extend them to the rows of a matrix \(T_0\in\operatorname{GL}_n(\mathbb R)\), preserving \((T_0)_{\mathsf O,:}=C\), and put \(W_0=T_0^{-1}\). The \((x,x)\)-entry of \(T_0W_0=I_n\) is
\[
 1=\sum_{j=1}^n C_{xj}(W_0)_{jx}. \tag{10}
\]
Thus some \(j\) has both \(C_{xj}\ne0\) and \((W_0)_{jx}\ne0\). The inverse-cofactor formula says that this latter inequality is equivalent to \(\det((T_0)_{-x,-j})\ne0\). Its \(p-1\) observed rows other than \(x\), namely the rows of \(C_{-x,-j}\), are therefore independent. Hence \(j\in J_x(C)\), proving nonemptiness.

Now fix any \(j\in J_x(C)\). We first justify the shear prescribed by \(\operatorname{Cert}\). Because the rows of \(C_{-x,:}\) are independent,
\[
 \operatorname{rank}(C_{-x,-j})<p-1
 \quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad
 e_j^\top\in\operatorname{rowspan}(C_{-x,:}). \tag{11}
\]
Indeed, a nonzero dependence after deletion gives a nonzero linear combination of the independent full rows supported only at coordinate \(j\), and hence a nonzero multiple of \(e_j^\top\); the converse follows by deleting coordinate \(j\). Row \(j\) of \(W_0\) is the unique coordinate vector of \(e_j^\top\) in the row basis of \(T_0\), since
\[
 e_j^\top=(e_j^\top W_0)T_0.
\]
Consequently (11) is also equivalent to
\[
 (W_0)_{jx}=0
 \quad\text{and}\quad
 (W_0)_{j\ell}=0\ \text{for every }\ell\in\mathsf L. \tag{12}
\]
The admissibility of \(j\) rules out (12). If \((W_0)_{jx}\ne0\), set \(T_j=T_0\) and \(W_j=W_0\). Otherwise (12) supplies \(\ell\in\mathsf L\) with \((W_0)_{j\ell}\ne0\). Since \(x\ne\ell\), the matrices \(I_n+e_\ell e_x^\top\) and \(I_n-e_\ell e_x^\top\) are inverse, so the prescribed shear satisfies
\[
 T_j=(I_n+e_\ell e_x^\top)T_0,
 \qquad
 W_j=W_0(I_n-e_\ell e_x^\top),
 \qquad
 (W_j)_{jx}=-(W_0)_{j\ell}\ne0. \tag{13}
\]
Only latent row \(\ell\) changes, hence \((T_j)_{\mathsf O,:}=C\), and \(T_j\) remains invertible.

Because \(T_j=W_j^{-1}\) and \((T_j)_{xj}=C_{xj}\ne0\), another inverse-cofactor identity gives
\[
 \det((W_j)_{-j,-x})\ne0. \tag{14}
\]
The determinant expansion in (14) contains a nonzero product. Its indices give a perfect matching from the source rows other than \(j\) to the equation columns other than \(x\). Augment it by assigning row \(j\) to column \(x\), and let \(\Pi_j\) permute the rows of \(W_j\) so that every diagonal entry of \(\Pi_jW_j\) is nonzero and row \(x\) is the old row \(j\). Set
\[
 D_j=\operatorname{diag}(\Pi_jW_j),
 \qquad Q_j=D_j^{-1}\Pi_jW_j,
 \qquad H_j=D_j^{-1}\Pi_j. \tag{15}
\]
Then \(D_j\) is invertible, \(Q_j\) is invertible with unit diagonal, and \(H_j\) is monomial. Moreover,
\[
 Q_j^{-1}H_j
 =W_j^{-1}\Pi_j^{-1}D_jD_j^{-1}\Pi_j
 =T_j, \tag{16}
\]
so \([Q_j^{-1}H_j]_{\mathsf O,:}=C\) and \(\mathcal L(C\varepsilon)=P_X\). The canonical sources \(\varepsilon_1,\ldots,\varepsilon_n\) are mutually independent, nonconstant, and non-Gaussian by the population assumptions, while the columns of \(C\) are nonzero and pairwise nonproportional. Thus all irreducible LiNG and observed-law requirements in the definition of \(\mathfrak F_x(P_X)\) hold.

The augmentation in (15) gives \((H_j)_{xj}\ne0\), so \(s_{\mathcal M_j}(x)=j\). From (16),
\[
 C_{xj}=(Q_j^{-1})_{xx}(H_j)_{xj}.
\]
Both \(C_{xj}\) and \((H_j)_{xj}\) are nonzero; hence \((Q_j^{-1})_{xx}\ne0\). The cofactor formula and invertibility of \(Q_j\) now give \(\det((Q_j)_{-x,-x})\ne0\). Therefore \(\mathcal M_j=(n,Q_j,H_j,\varepsilon)\) belongs to \(\mathfrak F_x(P_X)\). Applying the law-fiber response-rank lemma to this completion and using (16) proves both displayed response formulas.

For the operation count, Gaussian elimination extends the row basis and inverts \(T_0\) in \(O(n^3)\) arithmetic operations. Equivalence (12) classifies every deletion rank by scanning \(W_0\), in \(O(n^2)\) operations after the inverse. Each of at most \(n\) witnesses uses one \(O(n^2)\) shear, at most \(n\) augmenting-path searches each scanning at most \(n^2\) potential matching edges, and \(O(n^2)\) row normalization. Hence all witnesses require \(O(n^4)\) operations. This count uses exact zero tests in the real-arithmetic model; it is not a floating-point or bit-complexity statement. If \(C\) is rational, Gaussian elimination can choose a rational row-basis extension, and inversion, the integral shear, permutation, and divisions by the nonzero rational diagonal entries in (15) preserve rationality.

prose_updates.tldr: An observational law \(P_X\) with one normalized irreducible overcomplete-ICA representation \(X=C\varepsilon\) can support many cyclic latent LiNG mechanisms, but published irreducible-ICA uniqueness fixes their source count and mixing directions up to permutation and scaling. Over the full observational-law fiber of source-minimal one-shock-per-equation completions, the sharp response to one hard intervention is exactly the finite vector set \(\mathcal R_x^{\mathrm{vec}}(C)\); every scalar frontier is a coordinate projection. A latent-row shear and perfect matching construct an exact canonical same-law witness for every point in \(O(n^4)\) arithmetic operations. The separated iid layer supplies simultaneous uncertainty for this finite frontier, while the fourteen-stock Hong Kong series remains a population-level consumer unless dependent-time-series assumptions and empirical margins are separately certified.

project_justification.gap: Published irreducible-ICA results identify the source count and directions of an observational law up to permutation and scaling, and published latent cyclic LiNG work characterizes graph-level distributional equivalence or coefficients in specified graph classes. None characterizes the exact one-intervention response-vector image of every irreducible source-minimal completion of one numerical observational law.
project_justification.niche: Law-level ICA uniqueness makes deletion ranks and column ratios representation invariant, so a query-specific causal projection can be exact and far smaller than the compatible graph class without imposing dynamical stability.
project_justification.fill: The paper proves the sharp response-vector frontier, its scalar coordinate projections, exact canonical witnesses, vector and scalar point-identification certificates, polynomial-time enumeration, and a separated iid uncertainty layer.

sampling_model.design: Population identification conditions on the observational law \(P_X=\mathcal L(C\varepsilon)\) and ranges over every irreducible source-minimal one-shock-per-equation completion that entails that law and is solvable observationally and after intervention on \(x\). The inference layer uses observational iid sampling under \(P_X^{\otimes N}\) on the declared separated cumulant subclass.
sampling_model.units: \(N\) independent copies of the observed vector \(X\) under \(P_X^{\otimes N}\) for inference; no sampling condition is needed for the population law-fiber theorem.
sampling_model.treatment: A hard intervention replaces the structural equation for observed coordinate \(x\) by \(V_x=t\); the target is the joint response of all other observed coordinates to this one intervention, not a collection of jointly performed interventions.
sampling_model.overlap: Treatment-propensity overlap is not applicable. Population identification uses nonzero selected treatment loadings and deletion rank; uniform inference additionally uses the declared loading, minor, tensor, and separation margins.
sampling_model.nuisance_estimation: A normalized representative \(C\) is recovered up to column permutation and scaling from the observational law; the response-vector and scalar frontier maps are invariant to those indeterminacies. The separated iid construction estimates one common set of source directions, preserving the common source index across outcome coordinates.

prose_updates.related_work: ErikssonKoivunen2004 Theorem 3 is the primary all-non-Gaussian ICA identifiability result; DaiAlbrechtSpirtesZhang2026 Appendix B.1, Lemma 11 restates it for two irreducible representations as equality of source counts and mutual proportionality of mixing columns, and WangSeigal2026 records the same all-non-Gaussian no-collinear-columns criterion while developing the broader OICA benchmark. Those results supply law-level direction uniqueness, not the causal query projection. DaiAlbrechtSpirtesZhang2026 otherwise characterizes graph-indexed distribution families by children bases and perfect matchings; the present result instead maps every numerical same-law completion to a one-intervention response-vector frontier and constructs a full mechanism for every point. TramontanoKivvaSalehkaleybarDrtonKiyavash2024 gives complete acyclic graphical effect criteria, while TramontanoDrtonEtesami2026 gives partial cyclic coefficient criteria for known mixed graphs. LacerdaSpirtesRamseyHoyer2008 constructs square row-permutation candidates and distribution-entailment classes, but does not impose solvability after a selected intervention. BongersForrePetersMooij2021 supplies the distinction between observational and interventional solvability. The new contribution is the deletion-rank response image, its representation invariance, and exact canonical witnesses; published full-law ICA uniqueness is used as an antecedent.
prose_updates.technical_internal_limitation: The law fiber is deliberately restricted to irreducible source-minimal LiNG representations: every structural equation receives one distinct independent disturbance, and every observed mixing column is nonzero and pairwise nonproportional. Reducible representations, source splitting, duplicated or proportional directions, and extra shocks are excluded because they can change both source count and the causal frontier. This is the precise boundary of the law-invariance claim; it is not a claim over the larger graphically irreducible fiber at exceptional coefficients. No dynamical stability restriction is imposed. The vector set concerns all observed responses to one intervention with a common source witness, not Cartesian products across outcomes and not joint multiple interventions. Uniform root-\(N\) inference still requires denominator, minor, tensor, and separation margins. The fourteen-stock Hong Kong series is a population-certificate consumer only until serial dependence, mechanism changes, and empirical separation are addressed by a separate theorem and data certificate.
prose_updates.honest_scope: The population theorem covers the full observational-law fiber of irreducible source-minimal one-shock-per-equation cyclic LiNG completions with invertible observational and \(x\)-postintervention systems. It proves the finite response-vector frontier, all scalar coordinate projections, exact same-law witnesses, point-identification tests, and \(O(n^4)\) exact real-arithmetic certification without stability. Published irreducible-ICA uniqueness supplies the equality of source counts and directions up to permutation and scaling; only the law-conditioned causal deletion-rank projection and witness construction are new. Reducible, split-source, duplicated-direction, or proportional-column representations are outside scope, as are stability-refined fibers, Cartesian cross-outcome recombinations, joint multiple interventions, and dependent-time-series inference for the Hong Kong data. The separated iid inference results apply only on their explicit cumulant, loading, minor, and denominator margins.

payload.statement:
The set \(J_x(C)\) is nonempty. For every \(j\in J_x(C)\), \(\operatorname{Cert}(C,x)\) returns a canonical completion \(\mathcal M_j=(n,Q_j,H_j,\varepsilon)\in\mathfrak F_x(P_X)\) such that \(A^{\mathcal M_j}=C\), \(s_{\mathcal M_j}(x)=j\),
\[
 \boldsymbol\theta_{\leftarrow x}(\mathcal M_j)=\frac{C_{-x,j}}{C_{xj}},
 \qquad
 \theta_{y\leftarrow x}(\mathcal M_j)=\frac{C_{yj}}{C_{xj}}.
\]
All admissible indices and all these witnesses are computable in \(O(n^4)\) exact real-arithmetic operations. If \(C\) is rational, every returned \(Q_j\) and \(H_j\) is rational.
payload.proof_tex:
By full row rank, the \(p\) rows of \(C\) are independent. Extend them to the rows of a matrix \(T_0\in\operatorname{GL}_n(\mathbb R)\), preserving \((T_0)_{\mathsf O,:}=C\), and put \(W_0=T_0^{-1}\). The \((x,x)\)-entry of \(T_0W_0=I_n\) is
\[
 1=\sum_{j=1}^n C_{xj}(W_0)_{jx}. \tag{10}
\]
Thus some \(j\) has both \(C_{xj}\ne0\) and \((W_0)_{jx}\ne0\). The inverse-cofactor formula says that this latter inequality is equivalent to \(\det((T_0)_{-x,-j})\ne0\). Its \(p-1\) observed rows other than \(x\), namely the rows of \(C_{-x,-j}\), are therefore independent. Hence \(j\in J_x(C)\), proving nonemptiness.

Now fix any \(j\in J_x(C)\). We first justify the shear prescribed by \(\operatorname{Cert}\). Because the rows of \(C_{-x,:}\) are independent,
\[
 \operatorname{rank}(C_{-x,-j})<p-1
 \quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad
 e_j^\top\in\operatorname{rowspan}(C_{-x,:}). \tag{11}
\]
Indeed, a nonzero dependence after deletion gives a nonzero linear combination of the independent full rows supported only at coordinate \(j\), and hence a nonzero multiple of \(e_j^\top\); the converse follows by deleting coordinate \(j\). Row \(j\) of \(W_0\) is the unique coordinate vector of \(e_j^\top\) in the row basis of \(T_0\), since
\[
 e_j^\top=(e_j^\top W_0)T_0.
\]
Consequently (11) is also equivalent to
\[
 (W_0)_{jx}=0
 \quad\text{and}\quad
 (W_0)_{j\ell}=0\ \text{for every }\ell\in\mathsf L. \tag{12}
\]
The admissibility of \(j\) rules out (12). If \((W_0)_{jx}\ne0\), set \(T_j=T_0\) and \(W_j=W_0\). Otherwise (12) supplies \(\ell\in\mathsf L\) with \((W_0)_{j\ell}\ne0\). Since \(x\ne\ell\), the matrices \(I_n+e_\ell e_x^\top\) and \(I_n-e_\ell e_x^\top\) are inverse, so the prescribed shear satisfies
\[
 T_j=(I_n+e_\ell e_x^\top)T_0,
 \qquad
 W_j=W_0(I_n-e_\ell e_x^\top),
 \qquad
 (W_j)_{jx}=-(W_0)_{j\ell}\ne0. \tag{13}
\]
Only latent row \(\ell\) changes, hence \((T_j)_{\mathsf O,:}=C\), and \(T_j\) remains invertible.

Because \(T_j=W_j^{-1}\) and \((T_j)_{xj}=C_{xj}\ne0\), another inverse-cofactor identity gives
\[
 \det((W_j)_{-j,-x})\ne0. \tag{14}
\]
The determinant expansion in (14) contains a nonzero product. Its indices give a perfect matching from the source rows other than \(j\) to the equation columns other than \(x\). Augment it by assigning row \(j\) to column \(x\), and let \(\Pi_j\) permute the rows of \(W_j\) so that every diagonal entry of \(\Pi_jW_j\) is nonzero and row \(x\) is the old row \(j\). Set
\[
 D_j=\operatorname{diag}(\Pi_jW_j),
 \qquad Q_j=D_j^{-1}\Pi_jW_j,
 \qquad H_j=D_j^{-1}\Pi_j. \tag{15}
\]
Then \(D_j\) is invertible, \(Q_j\) is invertible with unit diagonal, and \(H_j\) is monomial. Moreover,
\[
 Q_j^{-1}H_j
 =W_j^{-1}\Pi_j^{-1}D_jD_j^{-1}\Pi_j
 =T_j, \tag{16}
\]
so \([Q_j^{-1}H_j]_{\mathsf O,:}=C\) and \(\mathcal L(C\varepsilon)=P_X\). The canonical sources \(\varepsilon_1,\ldots,\varepsilon_n\) are mutually independent, nonconstant, and non-Gaussian by the population assumptions, while the columns of \(C\) are nonzero and pairwise nonproportional. Thus all irreducible LiNG and observed-law requirements in the definition of \(\mathfrak F_x(P_X)\) hold.

The augmentation in (15) gives \((H_j)_{xj}\ne0\), so \(s_{\mathcal M_j}(x)=j\). From (16),
\[
 C_{xj}=(Q_j^{-1})_{xx}(H_j)_{xj}.
\]
Both \(C_{xj}\) and \((H_j)_{xj}\) are nonzero; hence \((Q_j^{-1})_{xx}\ne0\). The cofactor formula and invertibility of \(Q_j\) now give \(\det((Q_j)_{-x,-x})\ne0\). Therefore \(\mathcal M_j=(n,Q_j,H_j,\varepsilon)\) belongs to \(\mathfrak F_x(P_X)\). Applying the law-fiber response-rank lemma to this completion and using (16) proves both displayed response formulas.

For the operation count, Gaussian elimination extends the row basis and inverts \(T_0\) in \(O(n^3)\) arithmetic operations. Equivalence (12) classifies every deletion rank by scanning \(W_0\), in \(O(n^2)\) operations after the inverse. Each of at most \(n\) witnesses uses one \(O(n^2)\) shear, at most \(n\) augmenting-path searches each scanning at most \(n^2\) potential matching edges, and \(O(n^2)\) row normalization. Hence all witnesses require \(O(n^4)\) operations. This count uses exact zero tests in the real-arithmetic model; it is not a floating-point or bit-complexity statement. If \(C\) is rational, Gaussian elimination can choose a rational row-basis extension, and inversion, the integral shear, permutation, and divisions by the nonzero rational diagonal entries in (15) preserve rationality.

payload.statement:
For every \(\mathcal M=(m_{\mathcal M},Q,H,\xi^{\mathcal M})\in\mathfrak F_x(P_X)\), put \(A=A^{\mathcal M}\) and \(k=s_{\mathcal M}(x)\). Then
\[
 A_{xk}\ne0,
 \qquad \operatorname{rank}(A_{-x,-k})=p-1,
 \qquad \boldsymbol\theta_{\leftarrow x}(\mathcal M)=\frac{A_{-x,k}}{A_{xk}},
 \qquad \theta_{y\leftarrow x}(\mathcal M)=\frac{A_{yk}}{A_{xk}}.
\]
payload.proof_tex:
Fix \(\mathcal M\) in the stated fiber and abbreviate \(m=m_{\mathcal M}\). Membership in \(\mathfrak F_x(P_X)\) gives \(Q_{ii}=1\), monomial \(H\), \(\det(Q)\ne0\), and \(\det(Q_{-x,-x})\ne0\). Let \(k=s_{\mathcal M}(x)\) and \(h=H_{xk}\ne0\). Since \(H\) is monomial, its \(k\)-th column has no other nonzero entry, so
\[
 He_k=h e_x. \tag{4}
\]

First derive the hard-intervention response rather than identifying it with an observed quantity by definition. Under \(\operatorname{do}(V_x=t)\), the remaining equilibrium equations are
\[
 Q_{-x,-x}V_{-x}=H_{-x,:}\xi^{\mathcal M}-Q_{-x,x}t.
\]
The postintervention determinant condition permits inversion and differentiation, giving
\[
 \frac{\partial\,\operatorname{Eq}_{\mathcal M}(V_{-x}\mid\operatorname{do}(V_x=t))}{\partial t}
 =-Q_{-x,-x}^{-1}Q_{-x,x}. \tag{5}
\]
The cofactor formula and the two determinant conditions give
\[
 (Q^{-1})_{xx}=\frac{\det(Q_{-x,-x})}{\det(Q)}\ne0. \tag{6}
\]
Taking the rows other than \(x\) in \(QQ^{-1}e_x=e_x\) yields
\[
 Q_{-x,-x}(Q^{-1})_{-x,x}+Q_{-x,x}(Q^{-1})_{xx}=0.
\]
Division is legal by (6), and comparison with (5) proves
\[
 \boldsymbol\theta_{\leftarrow x}(\mathcal M)
 =\frac{(Q^{-1})_{-x,x}}{(Q^{-1})_{xx}}. \tag{7}
\]

Set \(T=Q^{-1}H\), so \(T\) is invertible and \(A=T_{\mathsf O,:}\). Equation (4) implies
\[
 T_{:,k}=h(Q^{-1})_{:,x}. \tag{8}
\]
In particular, (6) and \(h\ne0\) imply \(A_{xk}=h(Q^{-1})_{xx}\ne0\). Dividing the observed coordinates of (8) and using (7) gives the vector ratio, and taking coordinate \(y\) gives the scalar ratio.

It remains to prove the deletion rank. From (4), row \(k\) of \(H^{-1}\) is zero off column \(x\) and \((H^{-1})_{kx}=h^{-1}\). Therefore, using \(Q_{xx}=1\),
\[
 (T^{-1})_{kx}=(H^{-1}Q)_{kx}=h^{-1}Q_{xx}=h^{-1}\ne0. \tag{9}
\]
The inverse-cofactor formula applied to (9) shows \(\det(T_{-x,-k})\ne0\). Thus all rows of \(T_{-x,-k}\) are linearly independent. The \(p-1\) observed rows other than \(x\) form the submatrix \(A_{-x,-k}\), so those rows are independent and \(\operatorname{rank}(A_{-x,-k})=p-1\), as claimed.

payload.proof_tex:
Define the causal response-set target by the left side of (17); it ranges over structural mechanisms and is not defined to equal an observed-law functional. We prove its equality with the computable deletion-rank map on the right.

The canonical law-fiber witness lemma first gives \(J_x(C)\ne\varnothing\). For the necessity inclusion, fix an arbitrary \(\mathcal M\in\mathfrak F_x(P_X)\). By the cited irreducible-ICA law-uniqueness lemma, \(m_{\mathcal M}=n\) and
\[
 A^{\mathcal M}=C\Pi D \tag{19}
\]
for a permutation matrix \(\Pi\) and an invertible diagonal matrix \(D\). Write \(\Pi e_k=e_{\pi(k)}\), and let \(k=s_{\mathcal M}(x)\). The law-fiber response-rank lemma gives
\[
 A^{\mathcal M}_{xk}\ne0,
 \qquad \operatorname{rank}(A^{\mathcal M}_{-x,-k})=p-1,
 \qquad
 \boldsymbol\theta_{\leftarrow x}(\mathcal M)
 =\frac{A^{\mathcal M}_{-x,k}}{A^{\mathcal M}_{xk}}. \tag{20}
\]
The monomial-frontier invariance lemma applied to (19) turns (20) into
\[
 \pi(k)\in J_x(C),
 \qquad
 \boldsymbol\theta_{\leftarrow x}(\mathcal M)
 =\frac{C_{-x,\pi(k)}}{C_{x,\pi(k)}}
 \in\mathcal R_x^{\mathrm{vec}}(C). \tag{21}
\]
This proves the inclusion of the causal target in the observable functional for every completion of the observational law, not merely for a fixed source tuple.

For sufficiency, take any \(r\in\mathcal R_x^{\mathrm{vec}}(C)\). By definition, \(r=C_{-x,j}/C_{xj}\) for some \(j\in J_x(C)\). The canonical witness lemma constructs
\[
 \mathcal M_j=(n,Q_j,H_j,\varepsilon)\in\mathfrak F_x(P_X),
 \qquad A^{\mathcal M_j}=C,
 \qquad
 \boldsymbol\theta_{\leftarrow x}(\mathcal M_j)=r. \tag{22}
\]
Thus every value of the observable deletion-rank map is attained by a full structural completion having exactly the canonical representation. Equations (21)--(22) prove (17) and its sharpness over the whole law fiber.

For any completion, the definition of the scalar hard-intervention effect and the response-rank lemma give
\[
 \theta_{y\leftarrow x}(\mathcal M)
 =\operatorname{pr}_y\boldsymbol\theta_{\leftarrow x}(\mathcal M).
\]
Projecting both sides of (17) coordinatewise therefore proves (18); in particular, no Cartesian combination of effects from different source indices is introduced.

If distinct \(j,k\in J_x(C)\) had equal vector ratios, adjoining their common treatment coordinate \(1\) would give
\[
 \frac{C_{:,j}}{C_{xj}}=\frac{C_{:,k}}{C_{xk}}.
\]
Because both denominators are nonzero, this would make columns \(c_j\) and \(c_k\) proportional, contrary to the distinct-directions assumption. Hence the index-to-vector map is injective. Since \(J_x(C)\) is nonempty, the vector target is a singleton exactly when \(|J_x(C)|=1\).

For the scalar claim, the row of \(C_{\{x,y\},J_x(C)}\) indexed by \(x\) is nonzero entrywise. This two-row matrix has rank one if and only if
\[
 C_{xj}C_{yk}-C_{xk}C_{yj}=0
 \quad\text{for all }j,k\in J_x(C). \tag{23}
\]
Division by \(C_{xj}C_{xk}\ne0\) shows that (23) is equivalent to equality of all ratios \(C_{yj}/C_{xj}\), hence to \(|\mathcal R_{xy}(C)|=1\). By (18), this is exactly scalar point identification over the law fiber.

Finally, the canonical witness lemma computes every admissible index and its exact completion in \(O(n^4)\) operations and preserves rationality.
